title: The scale of homogeneity in DESI Data Release 1
authors: Cullan Howlett, L. Giani, Elizabeth G. O'Brien, A. Whitford, Tamara M. Davis, J. Aguilar, S. Ahlen, U. Andrade, E. Armengaud, S. BenZvi, F. Beutler, D. Bianchi, D. Brooks, R. Canning, A. Carnero Rosell, F. J. Castander, E. Chaussidon, T. Claybaugh, A. Cuceu, A. de la Macorra, Arjun Dey, Biprateep Dey, P. Doel, D. Forero-Sánchez, J. E. Forero-Romero, E. Gaztañaga, Satya Gontcho A Gontcho, G. Gutierrez, C. Hahn, K. Honscheid, D. Huterer, M. Ishak, S. Juneau, T. Karim, D. Kirkby, A. Kremin, O. Lahav, A. Lambert, C. Lamman, M. Landriau, L. Le Guillou, M. Manera, A. Meisner, R. Miquel, J. Moustakas, S. Nadathur, J. A. Newman, H. E. Noriega, E. Paillas, N. Palanque-Delabrouille, W. J. Percival, C. Poppett, F. Prada, I. Pérez-Ràfols, C. Ravoux, G. Rossi, R. Ruggeri, L. Samushia, E. Sanchez, C. Saulder, E. F. Schlafly, D. Schlegel, M. Schubnell, J. Silber, M. Siudek, G. Tarlé, B. A. Weaver, H. Zou
abstract: We present measurements of the scale of cosmic homogeneity using the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), the largest publicly available spectroscopic extragalactic survey to date. Using a counts-in-spheres estimator applied to nearly 5 million galaxies and quasars across six independent redshift bins spanning $0.1 < z < 2.1$, we measure the correlation dimension $D_2(r)$ and define the homogeneity scale $R_H$ as the point at which the galaxy distribution reaches within 1\% of the homogeneous asymptotic value. We find that all tracers clearly transition to homogeneity, with the galaxy homogeneity scale ranging from $93.8^{+0.9}_{-0.7}$ to $142.6^{+1.4}_{-1.4}$ $h^{-1}$Mpc depending on the tracer redshift, galaxy bias, and modelling used to extract the scale. Using a cosmology-dependent model, we reconstruct the underlying matter homogeneity scale, finding it decreases monotonically with redshift in excellent agreement with $\Lambda$CDM predictions. We identify a systematic offset of up to $\sim 10\%$ between measurements in the North and South Galactic Caps, largely due to fiber assignment effects reproduced in our simulations. Accounting for this, and with a complementary demonstration using toy models that our methodology correctly identifies inhomogeneous universes in all but rather finely-tuned observer configurations, this hence provides strong evidence in favour of the cosmological principle across our full redshift range. Our matter homogeneity scale measurements are consistent with, and substantially more precise than, previous constraints from WiggleZ and SDSS, demonstrating the power of DESI data for precision tests of the cosmological principle.
comments: 19 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to the Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia

figs.cap: The sky distribution of the DESI DR1 data used in this work (black points), compared to the distribution of dust in the Milky Way (coloured by E(B-V) as measured by Schlegel et al. 1998). The data at positive/negative Galactic latitudes (i.e., on the left/right-hand sides of the plot) are referred to as the North and South Galactic Caps (NGC/SGC) respectively. The patchiness of the DR1 data, and individual DESI tiles, are readily apparent, requiring us to make use of the random catalogues and systematics weights provided with the DESI large-scale structure catalogues when estimating the homogeneity scale.

Measurement of the correlation dimension as a function of scale for 4 different toy models, constructed by populating a box of edge-length 2$h^{-1}$Gpc with $10^{6}$ particles and measuring them using the estimator described in Section 3.1. The top and bottom figures shows measurements for observers placed at [0,0,0] $h^{-1}$Mpc and [-200,-200,-200] $h^{-1}$Mpc respectively. In both cases, the top inset panels show 200$h^{-1}$Mpc thick slices of the four distributions as a visual aid, where the white cross and circle shows the observer’s location and maximum distance cut used for the measurements. The solid lines show measurements using a fully uniform random catalogue. Dashed lines are produced using a ‘reshuffled’ random catalogue where the redshifts of the random points are generated by drawing from the data. The uniform and ‘Swiss Cheese’ models are clearly delineated as homogeneous and inhomogeneous respectively regardless of the choice of observer or random catalogue. The isotropic but inhomogeneous Gaussian and Giant Void models however can appear homogeneous depending on the observer’s proximity to the centre of the distribution when a ‘reshuffled’ random catalogue is used (as is done in our real DESI data).

Measurements of the mean scaled counts as a function of scale for each of the 6 DESI redshift bins considered in this work and both NGC and SGC sky areas (closed and open points respectively). Also shown are similar measurements for the Abacus-2 mocks, averaged over all 25 realisations, for both the NGC (solid lines) and SGC (dashed lines). The dotted horizontal line demarcates a $1\%$ deviation from the homogeneous expectation to guide the eye. In all cases we see that the data converges towards homogeneity on scales $\gtrsim 100h^{-1}$Mpc in a similar fashion as the $\Lambda$CDM-based mocks, but there are notable differences between the various tracers, sky areas, and between the mocks and data, which are investigated further using the correlation dimension.

Measurements of the correlation dimension as a function of scale for each of the 6 DESI redshift bins considered in this work for the NGC (closed points) and SGC (open points). Alongside the measurements we show the best-fit basis-spline models (solid lines for NGC and dashed lines for SGC), used to extract the quoted homogeneity scale $R^{\mathrm{galaxy}}_{H}$ for that galaxy sample. The constraints on this scale are highlighted as the colored vertical band and pair of dashed lines for the NGC and SGC respectively, and also included as text. The black dotted vertical lines show the range of scales included in our fits, discussed in Section 4, while the dotted and solid horizontal lines denote the values of $D_{2}(r)=2.97$ (1% homogeneity threshold) and the asymptotic homogeneity value $D_{2}(r)=3.0$ respectively. The homogeneity scale is defined as the point where the data crosses the dotted horizontal line. We see that all tracers and sky patches approach the expectations for homogeneous Universe, although with differences in the homogeneity scale between tracers and between sky patches for the same tracer.

Validation of the model-fitting procedure via constraints on the homogeneity scale of galaxies measured from Abacus-2 simulations for each DESI tracer. Closed and open points show constraints from the NGC and SGC sky patches respectively, with mock number labeled on the x-axis and the last, ‘star’, data point showing the fit to the mock mean using the covariance for a single realisation (i.e., the same covariance matrix as used for fits to the data). Horizontal bands show the standard deviation, centred on the mean, across the individual mock fits (filled band for NGC and dashed lines for SGC respectively). Note that the star, coming from fits to the mean data vector, and the center of the horizontal band, coming from the mean of the individual fits, need not agree — the good agreement hence validates our approach. The right-hand panels for each tracer show the best-fit $\chi^{2}$ for each of the individual fits, with filled and unfilled histograms used for the NGC and SGC sky patches respectively. The vertical dashed line shows the number of degrees of freedom for each tracer. In all cases, we see consistent differences in the results from the NGC and SGC for a given tracer across individual mocks and the mock mean, as would be expected if this was due to the fiber assignment process. Nonetheless, the results for the mock mean are consistent with the scatter between mocks and the $\chi^{2}$ for all but the QSO results are close to the number of degrees of freedom, indicating our estimated covariance matrices (and associated rescaling factors in Table 2) error bars are reliable. The high QSO $\chi^{2}$ is likely due to non-linear modelling inaccuracies, but this was not found in the fits to the real data.

Constraints on the matter homogeneity scale as a function of redshift. Coloured points show our new DESI DR1 constraints, following the same colour scheme as used elsewhere in this work and placed at the effective redshift of the tracer. Closed and open points show NGC and SGC sky patches respectively. Faint grey points are results from previous works using WiggleZ (Scrimgeour et al., 2012) and SDSS data (Ntelis et al., 2017; Gonçalves et al., 2018), rescaled to account for differences in the fiducial cosmology used in those works and here. The dashed line is the predicted homogeneity scale for our fiducial $\Lambda$CDM model, while the bottom panel plots ratios relative to this model.

title: Young Planets around Young Accreting Stars: II. Circumplanetary Disk Formation and Accretion
authors: Arturo Cevallos Soto, Zhaohuan Zhu
abstract: We present global 3-D ideal-MHD simulations of young giant planets in a protoplanetary disk (PPD) undergoing magnetospheric accretion onto its host star. Extending our previous work, we insert three planets with planet-to-star mass ratio \(q = 0.01\) (\(\sim 10\) Jupiter masses) at 0.45, 0.9, and 1.8 times the magnetospheric truncation radius, \(R_T\) , thereby probing the low-density cavity, disk-cavity boundary, and turbulent inner disk. The outermost two planets develop circumplanetary disks (CPDs), whereas the innermost planet forms no persistent bound structure because its high velocity relative to the magnetosphere reduces the effective Bondi radius below the planet's size. The outermost planet forms a stable, coplanar CPD whose inner region is rotationally supported and rotates at nearly the local Keplerian speed within \(\sim 0.25\) Hill radii. High-latitude inflow and midplane decretion produce meridional circulation and continuous recycling between the CPD and surrounding disk. Inflow through the Hill sphere is comparable to previous Hill-based hydrodynamic estimates. The middle planet, located near \(R_T\), develops a persistent polar CPD whose angular-momentum vector is parallel to the disk midplane, demonstrating that coherent circumplanetary structures can form within highly dynamic magnetospheric flows. Based on both the effective Bondi radius and thermal-mass criterion, we identify conditions under which massive giant planets form CPDs in the inner disk. Estimated planetary inflow accretion rates imply mass-doubling timescales \(\gtrsim 10\) Myr due to the low disk surface density, suggesting that, in the magnetically active zone, these planets undergo only limited late-stage growth before disk dispersal.
comments: 24 pages, 16 figures

title: Experimental Demonstration of Double-Fourier Interferometer Imaging for Future Space-Based Far-Infrared Observatories
authors: Jeremy P. Scott, Locke D. Spencer, Chris Benson, David Naylor, Berke Ricketti, Dinula De Silva, Vince Weiler
abstract: Far-infrared (FIR) astronomy is crucial for observing star formation, active galactic nuclei, and protoplanetary systems, but its effectiveness is severely limited by poor diffraction-limited spatial resolution. To overcome this limitation, a double-Fourier interferometer (DFI), which couples a spatial interferometer with a Fourier transform spectrometer, has been proposed to deliver high-resolution broadband spectral imaging. Despite various conceptual and prototype studies, a comprehensive demonstration of DFI capabilities has been lacking. In this study, we present the validation of key DFI observing techniques using a laboratory testbed operating in the 0.3 to 2.1 THz optical bandwidth. We detail the instrument's ideal response alongside necessary calibrations for intensity imbalances, non-linear phase errors, and phase-center offsets. Our experimental results successfully demonstrate aperture synthesis for both one- and two-dimensional targets, accurately recovering source geometries. Furthermore, we prove the instrument's sensitivity to spatially dependent spectral variations by utilizing a low-pass optical filter on extended sources. Finally, we validate wide-field imaging capabilities by combining data from independent pixels in a detector array, each sensitive to different regions of the source plane. The experimental data show significant agreement with theoretical predictions, with minor deviations attributed to optical aberrations and perspective effects. These laboratory demonstrations validate the DFI architecture as a highly capable and mature technology for future space-based FIR observatories.

title: Tayler Instability and Its Saturation in Rotating Stars
authors: Valentin Skoutnev, Andrei Beloborodov
abstract: In stably stratified regions of rotating stars, magnetic instabilities play a key role by enabling dynamo and angular momentum transport. In particular, the Tayler instability of wound-up toroidal fields has long been considered to drive the Tayler-Spruit dynamo. However, the nonlinear saturation of the instability is poorly understood, despite its central role in the dynamo loop. In this paper, we use global simulations to verify the recently completed linear theory of the Tayler instability and determine its saturation. We confirm the picture of overstability of magnetostrophic and inertial waves, which grow on similar magnetostrophic timescales but oscillate with different frequencies. We find that magnetostrophic waves saturate with large amplitudes $\delta B/B\sim 1$ and dissipate the toroidal field on magnetostrophic timescales, while inertial waves saturate with $\delta B/B\ll 1$ and erode the toroidal field over much longer timescales. Moreover, magnetostrophic waves efficiently regenerate axisymmetric poloidal fields through nonlinear couplings while inertial waves do not. Our results indicate that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo can operate only through the magnetostrophic wave branch and that its steady-state may follow the scenario proposed by \cite{spruit2002dynamo}, ruling out the small-amplitude saturation scenario proposed by \cite{fuller2019slowing}. Implications for angular momentum transport and magnetic field amplification in evolving stars and nascent neutron stars are discussed.
comments: Submitted to ApJ

title: Gravitational Wave Background from Metastable Current-Carrying Cosmic Strings
authors: Ivan Rybak, Rinku Maji, Qaisar Shafi
abstract: We study the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) generated by networks of current-carrying metastable cosmic strings (MSCSs). Extending previous studies, we include the possibility of vorton formation phenomenologically. We construct an analytical template that provides a fast and accurate approximation to the spectrum in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). We also show how the parameters of cosmic string networks determine the low-frequency slope. For the frequency range relevant for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK), we derive an analytical expression that constrains the scale-invariant part of the SGWB. Finally, we confront the model with current constraints from PTAs and the LVK collaboration. We identify regions of the parameter space that can produce a signal consistent with PTA observations but are in tension with LVK constraints, suggesting that additional mechanisms to suppress the high-frequency spectrum are required for a consistent interpretation of the PTA signal
comments: 44 pages, 14 figures

figs.cap: SGWB produced by MSCSs without current, illustrating the impact of varying the model parameters. In particular, the figure shows the effect of varying the loop size, string tension, and decay parameter $\kappa_{d}$, demonstrating how these parameters modify the low-frequency spectral slope of the SGWB, with spectral index $q=4/3$, $\mathcal{F}=0.1$ and $\alpha_{T}\equiv\zeta\alpha$

The spectra are shown for different values of the string tension, charge amplitude $Y$, vector coupling $e^{2}$, and $P_{\rm vort}$. The dashed lines indicate the power laws $f^{3}$ and $f^{2}$. Compared with the standard MSCSs, current-carrying strings exhibit both a shift in the characteristic frequency and a change in the spectral amplitude. For the parameters considered here, vorton formation predominantly affects the high-frequency part of the spectrum, while leaving the low-frequency behavior nearly unchanged. Following [145], we take the spectral index to be $q=4/3$ for $Y=0$ and $q=5/3$ for $Y\neq 0$.

title: Turbulent gas-rich discs at high redshift: Chaotic orbits and rapid bulge formation at high gas fraction
authors: Johan M. Villa-Alatorre, Joss Bland-Hawthorn, Thor Tepper-Garcia, Oscar Agertz, Christoph Federrath
abstract: Using the \nexus\ N-body/hydrodynamic framework, we show that stellar bars that emerge in high-redshift disc galaxies are different in their orbital characteristics compared to their low-redshift counterparts. We identify bar-supporting orbits and, among them, find the fraction of chaotic orbits compared to regular orbits ($f_{\rm chaos}$). This fraction rises above 60\% for models with $f_{\rm gas} > 60 \%$; for $f_{\rm gas} \lesssim 60\%$, we observe chaotic fractions close to zero. The emerging bars seen in the $f_{\rm gas}= 80\%$ and $100\%$ simulations collapse in $\lesssim$1 Gyr to form central bulges supported by rotation, and this collapse follows soon after the chaotic fraction starts to dominate ($f_{\rm chaos} \gtrsim 50\%)$. Moreover, the gravitational potential in those simulations steepens rapidly over that period, and by integrating the chaotic orbits, we find that orbits that deviate from the evolving mean field are more likely to be chaotic. Hence, we argue that the irregularity associated with the rapidly evolving, central potentials drives higher chaotic fractions in these gas-rich bars. As a result, the emergent bars collapse through `violent relaxation' to form oblate rotating bulges. Supporting evidence for this picture comes from the fact that particles of different mass share identical radial profiles, a natural consequence of the rapid relaxation process.
comments: 14 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to MNRAS

title: Model of the instrumental polarization induced by a rotating HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures for CMB polarimetry
authors: Ryota Takaku, Hiroaki Imada, Guillaume Patanchon, Yuki Sakurai
abstract: Future CMB polarization experiments require precise control of instrumental systematics in the search for primordial $B$-mode polarization. A rotating half-wave plate (HWP) provides effective polarization modulation, but its non-ideal electromagnetic response can generate HWP-synchronous instrumental polarization. In this work, we characterize the response of a multi-layer sapphire HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures (SWS) using rigorous coupled-wave analysis. For three asymmetric SWS models, we find no substantial differences in the transmittance, polarization efficiency, or instrumental-polarization response that can be attributed to the type of SWS asymmetry. The fourth-harmonic instrumental polarization relevant to CMB polarization reconstruction is typically of order $10^{-4}$ in the CMB bands, which is expected to be mitigated. We further evaluate an actually fabricated SWS geometry, whose asymmetry enhances the retardance, and compare its response with that of an idealized model having the same type of asymmetry. Comparison of the realistic SWS with the idealized model shows that higher transmittance tends to be associated with lower instrumental polarization. These results suggest that improving the total transmission, including the effect of the fabricated SWS profile, may be more important for reducing HWP-induced instrumental polarization than tuning the SWS asymmetry itself.

title: Unveiling the Shock-Excited Molecular Environment in the Orion Protostar HOPS 370
authors: Somnath Dutta, Koshvendra Singh, Devendra K Ojha, Saurabh Sharma, Tarak Chand, Manojit Chakraborty, Kartik Gokhe, Joe P. Ninan, Jyotirmoy Dey
abstract: We present near-infrared K-band ($1.94$--$2.52~\mu$m) spectroscopy of the deeply embedded protostellar source HOPS\,370, obtained with the TIFR--ARIES Near Infrared Spectrometer (TANSPEC) on the 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). The spectrum is dominated by prominent molecular hydrogen ($\rm H_2$) ro-vibrational emission, with multiple transitions detected from the $1$--$0$ S, $2$--$1$ S, and $1$--$0$ Q branches. Using the intrinsically linked $\rm H_2$ $1$--$0$ Q(3) and $1$--$0$ S(1) transitions, which arise from the same upper energy level, we derive a visual extinction of $A_V = 23.24 \pm 1.25$ mag, corresponding to $A_K = 2.50 \pm 0.13$ mag, consistent with the embedded Class~0/I nature of the source. The diagnostic line ratio $F(2$--$1~{\rm S}(1))/F(1$--$0~{\rm S}(1)) = 0.12 \pm 0.01$ is consistent with thermal excitation and disfavors ultraviolet fluorescence as the dominant excitation mechanism. Assuming optically thin emission and local thermodynamic equilibrium, we derive an $\rm H_2$ excitation diagram that yields an excitation temperature of $2078 \pm 215$ K and a molecular hydrogen column density of $(1.93 \pm 0.93)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$. We further derive an ortho-to-para ratio of $2.45 \pm 0.21$, indicating substantial shock-driven thermal processing while remaining below the high-temperature equilibrium value of 3. Taken together, these diagnostics indicate that the molecular hydrogen emission in HOPS\,370 originates predominantly in warm, shock-heated gas most likely associated with its protostellar outflow. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combined S- and Q-branch $\rm H_2$ spectroscopy for constraining the physical conditions and excitation history of deeply embedded protostellar systems.
comments: 4 figures, 12 pages; accepted for publication in the Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy (JoAA)

title: A Spectral-model-independent Diagnostic of Phase-resolved Spectral Convergence in Swift J0243.6+6124
authors: Bo-Yan Chen, Peng-Ju Wang, Shu Zhang, Ling-Da Kong, Long Ji, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Hua Feng, Yu-Peng Chen, Ming-Yu Ge, Jing-Qiang Peng, Qing-Cang Shui, Wen-Zhong Li
abstract: We introduce a spectral-model-independent spectral-shape metric, $\delta_{\rm rms}$, to probe phase-resolved spectral evolution in the Galactic ultraluminous X-ray pulsar Swift J0243.6+6124. The $\delta_{\rm rms}$--luminosity relation reveals a reproducible convergence--redivergence behavior: spectra from two geometrically opposite pulse phases converge to near identity around $L_{\rm t}^{\ast}\sim8.8\times10^{37}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with a mean shape difference of only $\sim2\%$, and rediverge at higher luminosities, most prominently at higher energies. This strong phase-resolved spectral convergence coincides with a pulse-profile reversal and traces the same transition luminosities previously identified from broadband continuum evolution, including $L_{\rm t}\sim4.5\times10^{37}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$. These results suggest a possible luminosity-driven reweighting between a broadly distributed surface-reprocessed/reflected component and an increasingly important direct accretion-column contribution, while establishing $\delta_{\rm rms}$ as a robust, spectral-model-independent diagnostic of radiation-geometry restructuring in bright accreting X-ray pulsars.
comments: 9 pages, 7 figures (4 main-text figures and 3 appendix figures)

title: Age-Resolved Vertical Motions in the Milky Way Warp: A Localized Enhancement in Intermediate-Age Populations
authors: Xiaoyue Zhou, Xiaodian Chen, Haifeng Wang, Shu Wang, Zhihong He, Licai Deng
abstract: Determining how the Milky Way warp evolves provides constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of galactic disks. Using Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment Data Release 19 (APOGEE DR19) spectroscopy, we estimate ages for 222,355 red giants. With Gaia astrometry and geometric distances, we analyze 168,824 of these stars in five age bins spanning $0$--$10$ Gyr. The warp-related radial vertical-velocity ($V_Z$) profile of young red giants ($0$--$2$ Gyr) is broadly consistent with those of classical Cepheids and young open clusters. Over $9\leq R<12$ kpc, we find that the mean $V_Z$ values of the intermediate-age red giants ($2$--$4$ and $4$--$6$ Gyr) are $1.48\pm0.46$ and $1.49\pm0.52$ km s$^{-1}$ higher than that of the young population, respectively. By contrast, at $R\simeq12$--$13$ kpc, the $V_Z$ profiles of the $0$--$6$ Gyr red giants are consistent within their uncertainties. The intermediate-age enhancement persists across our robustness tests and may reflect smaller effective kinematic warp onset radii for the intermediate-age populations. The observed velocity differences may arise from the combined effects of earlier perturbations and the present-day warp, or from differences in vertical structure among stellar populations.

title: Asteroseismic properties of young pulsators in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. Discovery of period-spacing patterns in HD 281229
authors: Saakshi Wadhwa, Dario J. Fritzewski, Gang Li, Simon J. Murphy
abstract: Very young pulsating stars, including pre-main sequence pulsators, provide a rare opportunity to probe stellar interiors and investigate rotation during the earliest phases of stellar evolution. However, they remain relatively unexplored, particularly in the intermediate-mass regime. We aim to identify and characterise young pulsating stars in the Perseus Molecular Cloud using photometric data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). We compiled Gaia-based membership catalogues for the Perseus Molecular Cloud, applied selection criteria to isolate young intermediate-mass stars, and extracted light curves from TESS full-frame images. Variability classification was performed using Lomb-Scargle periodograms and iterative pre-whitening. For confirmed pressure-mode pulsators, we estimated the frequency of maximum pulsation power, $\nu_{\mathrm{max}}$. For gravity-mode candidates, we searched for period-spacing patterns and fit them using the traditional approximation of rotation. From 148 membership-selected targets, we identified eight pressure-mode pulsators and two objects showing possible gravity-mode pulsations. We analysed the previously known $\delta$ Sct star V705 Per, bringing the total sample to 149 targets. One of the gravity-mode pulsators, HD 281229, is the youngest star known to date with a detected and modelled period-spacing pattern. By simultaneously fitting the dipole and quadrupole period-spacing patterns, we estimate an asymptotic period spacing of $\Pi_0=4776\pm400$ s and a near-core rotation frequency of $f_{\mathrm{rot}}=1.317\pm0.05$ $\mathrm{d}^{-1}$. These results highlight the potential of asteroseismology to probe the internal structure and rotation of very young stars. The detected period-spacing pattern in HD 281229 shows that gravity-mode asteroseismology can provide meaningful constraints on the properties of stars at early evolutionary stages.

title: Machine Learning Based Classification of Type 1 Active Galactic Nuclei
authors: Jie Li, Xu-Liang Fan
abstract: Aims. We aim to provide a machine learning based method to distinguish type 1 quasars and type 1 Seyfert galaxies based on photometric data, which could be applied to large all-sky surveys. The method can also be used to obtain relatively complete samples of Seyfert galaxy candidates when broad-line AGNs have been selected. Results. The results of PCA show that quasars and Seyfert galaxies are partial distinguishable. The supervised classifier based on random forest (RF) achieves good performances for type 1 quasars with a F1 score of 0.967. The performance for classifying Seyfert galaxies is worse, with a F1 score of 0.791. Increasing the classification threshold can help to derive a sample of Seyfert galaxies with high purity. The classifier are then applied to the cross-matched sample with DESI DR1. When compared with the results of spectroscopic classification, quasars also show high precision and recall. For Seyfert galaxies identified by RF classifier, there are plenty of less luminous sources who are classified as quasars by spectroscopic method. If they are regarded as Seyfert galaxies, our classifier also performs well to predict Seyfert galaxies. Both the median SEDs and the fraction of Seyfert galaxies derived by our classifier are similar with those for the training sample, while the fraction of Seyfert galaxies for spectroscopic classification are lower at all redshift. These results indicate that our classifier can recover the features of Seyfert galaxies, at least those similar to the Seyfert galaxies in the training sample.
comments: 14 Figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in A&A

title: NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's First View of the Neptune Trojan L5 (Trailing) Cloud: Two New Long-Term Stable Trojans
authors: Megan E. Schwamb, Pedro H. Bernardinelli, Kathryn Volk, Joseph Murtagh, Hsing Wen Lin, Andrew S. Rivkin, Colin Orion Chandler, R. Lynne Jones, Susan D. Benecchi, Mario Jurić, Jacob A. Kurlander, Sarah Greenstreet, Adam Wilson, Maxine West, Ryan R. Lyttle
abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's combination of survey speed, sky coverage, and depth provides a unique opportunity to study the distant Trans-Neptunian region, including the Neptune Trojans. The Neptune Trojans are small bodies on orbits with Neptune's semimajor axis that are locked in the 1:1 mean motion resonance librating about the ice giant's stable Lagrange points, L4 (leading) and L5 (trailing), located 60$^{\circ}$ ahead of or behind the planet. For more than 15 years, the on-sky location of the L5 Neptune Trojan cloud has been coincident with the Galactic plane and Galactic center; the high stellar density has significantly hindered the discovery of L5 Neptune Trojans. In 2025, the L5 cloud has now moved sufficiently out of the galactic plane to overlap with the sky covered by Rubin Observatory's Science Validation (SV) survey that was executed during the Observatory's commissioning phase. We report on two new confirmed long-term stable (primordial) members of the Neptune L5 Trojan cloud (2025 MH348 and 2025 NN80), doubling the known sample, and one candidate (2025 MD138) that have been found in a preliminary search of the SV survey observations. We present our study to characterize the physical and dynamical properties of these objects and compare the L5 sample to the well-studied L4 cloud. This work also presents the first characterization of objects discovered by Rubin Observatory's moving object discovery pipelines using observations taken in an LSST-like cadence and as such, provides a blueprint for LSST-era analyses.

title: Numerical Simulations of the interaction between winds from tidal disruption event and supermassive black hole circumnuclear medium
authors: De-Fu Bu, Yu-Heng Sheng, Liang Chen, Guo-Bin Mou, Hao-Jie Xia, Xiao-Hong Yang
abstract: The interaction between winds from tidal disruption event (TDE) and the circumnuclear medium (CNM) around supermassive black holes is believed to contribute to the radio emission of non-jetted TDEs. This model has been studied both analytically and numerically. In previous works, the properties of wind are usually set to be angle-independent. It is not clear to what extent the results deviate from those in the case where TDE wind properties are angle-dependent. We perform numerical simulations to investigate the effects of the angular distribution of wind properties on the radio light curve in the wind-CNM interaction model. We find that given that the wind mass and kinetic energy fixed, the radio light curve in the optically thin waveband significantly depends on the angle-dependence of wind properties. Even when the swept-up CNM mass is still less than the wind mass, a slight deceleration can affect the light curve. Changing the angular dependence of the wind properties causes the deceleration to vary across angles. Consequently, the final light curve--the time evolution of radiation integrated over all angles--would differ significantly from that predicted in models with a spatially uniform wind injection. This can result in a slower rise or a faster decline (depending on the CNM profile) than the analytical prediction, and can even turn the rise phase into a long-lasting plateau. Therefore, it is essential to carefully take into account the angular dependence of wind properties to study the wind-CNM interaction.

title: Characterisation of the ILMT 4K x 4K TDI CCD imager
authors: Gokul singh Mehra, Bhavya Ailawadhi, Talat Akhunov, Monalisa Dubey, Naveen Dukiya, Sara Filali, Paul Hickson, Priyanshi Kumari, Kuntal Misra, Vibhore Negi, Kumar Pranshu, Jean Surdej, Sarvesh Kumar Yadav
abstract: In this work, we determine the gain and read-out noise of the 4Kx4K CCD imager used with the 4-m International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT). Due to the zenith-pointing characteristic of the telescope, the CCD operates in the Time Delay Integration (TDI) mode for image acquisition. The CCD frames obtained during rising twilight have non-uniform illumination and can potentially be used to calculate important CCD parameters using two approaches. The first approach directly measures variance in flux along rows with minimum horizontal gradient, despite the strong vertical illumination gradient. The second method divides the CCD frame into regions exposed to similar background illumination and analyses the flux ratio variation between the two regions. Mathematically, we establish a linear relationship between the signal variance and average flux, from which gain is determined, while the read-out noise (RON) is measured independently from the bias frames. Both methods provide a gain value of approximately 3.9 e/ADU, while the RON measured from bias frames is 1.55 ADU (~ 6 e). Estimation of these parameters provides a better understanding of the CCD performance and allows for an accurate calibration.

title: Gravitational Dark Matter Production from Spectator Field in $R^2$-Higgs Inflation
authors: Arnab Samanta, Rajesh Mondal, Tanmoy Modak
abstract: We investigate the cosmological gravitational dark matter production of spectator field $\chi$ in the multifield $R^2$-Higgs inflation. The spectator field $\chi$ couples to gravity only through a non-minimal coupling $\xi_\chi\chi^2R$ and serves as a dark matter (DM) candidate. Working consistently in the Einstein frame, we derive the equation of motion of the background fields and fluctuations at linear order using the doubly covariant formalism. We show the dark matter production and the subsequent comoving relic abundance heavily depend on this effective mass of the field $\chi$. Specifically, we find that there exists cancellation regions in the effective mass-squared of $\chi$, which ensures the correct relic abundance is achieved. Further, we show that the preheating from Higgs and Goldstone may play critical role in accounting the observed relic density.

title: PyMsOfa 2.0: A Pure-Python Implementation of the IAU Standards of Fundamental Astronomy Service
authors: Dongjie Tan, Jianghui Ji, Jiacheng Liu
abstract: Astrometric calculations require authoritative algorithms so that every result is correct and reproducible. The Standards of Fundamental Astronomy (SOFA) service of the International Astronomical Union (IAU) provides such algorithms, officially released only in Fortran 77 and ANSI C. In an earlier paper we presented the first version of PyMsOfa, a Python package wrapping the SOFA C library. Here we present PyMsOfa 2.0, which re-implements the complete SOFA library in pure Python with NumPy. All 247 official SOFA routines are ported directly to Python, requiring no compilation of any external C library and running identically on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The routines operate on NumPy arrays, so arguments can be processed in batch, which is convenient for survey pipelines and Monte Carlo simulations. The package also provides an extension module with validated models not yet part of the official SOFA release, such as the improved precession--nutation model IAU 2006$_{J_2}$/2000A$_{R26}$. The reimplementation reproduces the official SOFA algorithms: all constants, series, and coefficients are taken unchanged from the SOFA source files, and routine names differ only by the pym prefix. We verify every routine against the official SOFA C release: most reproduce the C results to machine precision, the remainder within the accuracy tolerance stated in the SOFA documentation. The package has been applied to Gaia astrometric reduction and used in astrometric studies of the Closeby Habitable Exoplanet Survey (CHES) mission, and is available through PyPI, GitHub, and Zenodo.

title: The Ubiquity of White-Light Flares on the Sun
authors: Shuanghong Li, Yongliang Song, Kun Wang, Mei Zhang, Xianyong Bai, Xiao Yang
abstract: White-light flares (WLFs) have long been considered rare on the Sun, as most magnetic reconnections occur in the corona, making it difficult to transport sufficient energy downward to heat the very low layers for WL continuum emission. However, it is also argued that WL continuum emission is a common feature of all flares, and the rare detection of them is largely due to the limited sensitivity and resolution of telescopes. Recently, we developed a new method to identify WLFs, which exhibits extraordinary detection capability. Combined with SDO/HMI's over 15 years of continuous photospheric observations, it provides us an unprecedented opportunity to address the long-standing debate about WLF ubiquity. A total of 1951 flares (547 B-class, 1316 C-class, and 88 M-class) from 769 low-activity active regions (ARs; flare number $<$ 10) observed during January 2011 - May 2025 are investigated. Among these, 1012 are identified as WLFs, giving an overall occurrence rate of 51.9\%. The occurrence rates for B-, C-, and M-class flares are 36.9\%, 56.9\%, and 85.2\%, respectively, showing a clear increase with flare class. The occurrence rate is also highly correlated with the AR's sunspot number. For the first time, we find that WL continuum radiation is widely present even among B-class flares. Different WLFs contain varying numbers of WL kernels, which exhibit distinct properties, evolutionary behaviors and different relationships with GOES soft X-ray flux and its time derivative. These results strongly suggest that WLFs are a common phenomenon on the Sun.

title: Migration Traps as Variability Attractors. II. Nonmonotonic X-Ray Timing Signatures of Embedded Stellar-Mass Black Holes in AGN Disks
authors: Jing-Tong Xing, Tong Liu, Mouyuan Sun, Zhen-Yi Cai, Ya-Ping Li, Shuying Zhou, Da-Bin Lin, Jian-Min Wang
abstract: Stellar-mass black holes (sBHs) embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks may affect X-ray variability through magnetic reconnection. As sBHs migrate and accumulate near migration traps, they disturb the disk magnetic field and trigger reconnection events that heat the disk and eject plasma into the overlying corona. The injected plasma dissipates kinetic energy and can trigger the release of magnetic energy already stored in the corona. We calculate the resulting coronal X-ray emission and the disk ultraviolet (UV) variability, including the disk thermal response and reprocessing of incident X-rays. We find that embedded sBHs can initially enhance short-timescale X-ray variability, but the variability becomes suppressed as more sBHs accumulate in the disk. At higher mass accretion rates through AGN disks, this suppression appears earlier. As sBH-associated reconnection events become more frequent, their active regions increasingly overlap, reducing the magnetic energy available to each event from the corona. We also find that variations in the disk ultraviolet (UV) emission follow the X-ray variations with a shorter delay than in the model without sBHs. These results suggest that a growing population of embedded sBHs does not necessarily produce stronger short-timescale X-ray variability.
comments: 12 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables

figs.cap: Schematic diagram of the disk-corona energy transfer in our model. Magnetic reconnection associated with embedded sBHs ejects plasma from the AGN disk, while part of the released energy remains in the disk and contributes to local heating. The ejected plasma carries kinetic energy $K_{\rm up}$ into the corona, where collisions with coronal gas dissipate energy $E_{\rm sh}$ and may trigger further magnetic reconnection. The ordinary coronal energy input $E_{\rm bg,input}$ is divided between replenishing the stored magnetic energy $U_{B}$ and ordinary dissipation $E_{\rm bg,diss}$. Magnetic reconnection triggered by plasma impact transfers magnetic energy $E_{B,\rm com}$ from $U_{B}$ to $E_{\rm arc}$, which is gradually released as $E_{B,\rm rel}$. A fraction $\eta_{\rm X}$ of the dissipated energy, $E_{\rm bg,diss}+E_{\rm sh}+E_{B,\rm rel}$, contributes to the 0.3–10 keV X-ray emission. Part of the X-ray emission irradiates the disk and contributes to the UV/optical response.

title: Nongravitational Motion of 3I/ATLAS Far from the Sun: Robust Detection, Weak Constraints on the Activity Law
authors: Małgorzata Królikowska, Federico Spada, Luke Dones
abstract: 3I/ATLAS provides an unprecedented astrometric data set for studying nongravitational (NG) effects in an interstellar object, but existing orbital solutions depend strongly on assumptions regarding the heliocentric activity law and the treatment of the astrometric data. We investigate the extent to which astrometric observations constrain the heliocentric dependence of the NG activity function, focusing on the identifiability of different functional forms of $g(r)$ within standard NG orbit-determination frameworks. Astrometric observations obtained at heliocentric distances larger than 3.49 au before perihelion and 2.67 au after perihelion were analysed. Purely gravitational and nongravitational orbital solutions were determined using several activity laws, including the standard water-ice sublimation law and flatter more volatile ice prescriptions. The resulting residual distributions were evaluated using normality tests and analyses of temporal trends in the observed-minus-calculated residuals. The distant pre-perihelion observations are well described by a purely gravitational (GR) orbit, whereas the distant post-perihelion data exhibit a statistically significant non-Gaussian residual distribution under the GR model. When the distant pre- and post-perihelion observations are combined, nongravitational acceleration becomes clearly detectable through a significant reduction in the residual rms and the disappearance of systematic residual trends. However, the astrometric data do not uniquely distinguish between the tested activity laws: standard water-ice, more volatile and extreme volatile prescriptions produce statistically comparable orbital fits despite their markedly different heliocentric dependences. The existence of nongravitational acceleration is therefore considerably better constrained by astrometry than its physical origin or heliocentric dependence.
comments: 11 pages, 2 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics

title: The Influence of Hubble Expansion on the Future Merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda
authors: Yufan Zhou, Tianchi Zhang, Shihong Liao, Zhiyuan Li, Lan Wang, David Benisty
abstract: Most existing idealized simulations of galaxy mergers neglect Hubble expansion, as the local Hubble flow is curved by overdensities and the expansion effect is weak at these scales. However, even in the gravity-dominated Local Group (LG), the expansion itself still persists, and it has been shown important in some LG-related studies. Here we take the future merger of the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31) as a case study to investigate the differences between simulations with and without Hubble expansion. We perform a suite of idealized N-body simulations of the MW--M31 system under pure Newtonian, $\Lambda$CDM, and $w_0w_a$CDM scenarios, testing different masses and proper motions of galaxies informed by current observational constraints. At low M31 tangential velocities, especially in cases where the two galaxies merge within a Hubble time, the expansion effect is negligible; while at high velocities (>66.5 km/s), the $\Lambda$CDM simulations introduce a noticeable delay in the merger time compared to the Newtonian ones and may even alter the final fate of the system, but the caveat here is that the isolated-pair idealization and the assumed expansion history break down. The delay is also present but less pronounced in the $w_0w_a$CDM runs. When M33 and the Large Magellanic Cloud are included, the differences in merger times are reduced. In summary, Hubble expansion can play a noticeable role for galaxy mergers with high tangential velocities, but its actual influence on the MW--M31 merger depends on the precise masses and proper motions to be determined in the future.
comments: 10 pages (+3 pages appendix). Resubmitted to ApJ after referee's report

title: Coupled evolution of Earth's H2-rich proto-atmosphere and oxidized magma ocean: Efficient H2O production through dissolved H2 transport and atmospheric buffering of the magma ocean redox state
authors: Tatsuya Yoshida, Kirara Arima, Naoki Terada, Takeshi Kuroda, Kiyoshi Kuramoto
abstract: Giant impacts during Earth's final accretion likely generated global magma oceans, where the disproportionation of Fe^2+ at lower-mantle pressures and segregation of the resulting metallic iron into the core could have oxidized the magma ocean. Earth may nevertheless have had an H2-rich proto-atmosphere in chemical disequilibrium with the magma ocean, but the chemical coupling between this atmosphere and an oxidized magma ocean remains poorly constrained. Here we develop a coupled atmosphere-interior evolution model that includes diffusive transport in the boundary layer between the magma ocean and atmosphere, redox reactions in the melt, partitioning of oxide components and H2O among coexisting phases, and planetary cooling through a proto-atmosphere, with metallic iron produced by Fe^2+ disproportionation removed into the core as it forms. Atmospheric H2 transport into the magma ocean and subsequent H2O production become more efficient with increasingly frequent boundary layer renewal driven by buoyant overturn of dense melt cooled at the surface, allowing the atmosphere and magma ocean to chemically equilibrate within ~10^4 yr when the magma ocean is sufficiently deep and hot to extend into the lower mantle. Redox exchange with the atmosphere buffers the solidification-driven redox evolution of the magma ocean, preventing extreme oxidation or reduction of the coupled system. These results suggest that the coupled evolution could have contributed to early Earth's water inventory while maintaining a reducing H2-rich atmosphere.
comments: Published in The Planetary Science Journal

figs.cap: Schematic overview of the coupled atmosphere-interior evolution model. This model considers the diffusion of atmospheric H$_{2}$ into the magma ocean, redox reactions in the magma ocean, partitioning of oxide components and H$_{2}$O among each phase, and the cooling through the thermal planetary radiation, with Fe produced by Fe$^{2+}$ disproportionation removed into the core as it forms. Cases 1 and 2 represent two end-member treatments of material exchange between the magma ocean and solid mantle, introduced to account for uncertainty in the efficiency of material exchange between these reservoirs. Case 1 assumes efficient material exchange and equilibrium partitioning of oxide components and H$_{2}$O between the bulk magma ocean and solid mantle with uniform chemical compositions. Case 2 assumes inefficient material exchange, in which melt is efficiently trapped in the rheological transition region without subsequent material mixing in the solid mantle. The melt-side boundary layer at the interface between the magma ocean and atmosphere is considered to evaluate the H$_{2}$ diffusion rate into the magma ocean, with its overturn frequency determined by buoyancy-driven convective instability.

title: Understanding the origin of silver in metal-poor stars based on the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium analysis of Ag I lines
authors: Lyudmila Mashonkina, Tatyana Sitnova, Svetlana A. Yakovleva, Vera A. Vasil'eva
abstract: Silver is a poorly observed neutron-capture element, and understanding its Galactic production history requires accurate abundances for stellar samples covering a broad metallicity range. We refined the method for calculating stellar Ag abundances by considering the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) line formation for Ag I. A comprehensive model atom of silver was built from the atomic data available in the literature, including recent data on inelastic Ag I + H I collisions. We derived abundances using the high-resolution spectra and the synthetic spectrum method with the one-dimensional model atmospheres. From two Ag I lines in the solar spectrum we obtained the NLTE abundances log epsilon = 1.15 and 1.10 for different treatments of collisions with hydrogen atoms. The NLTE abundances of Ag were determined for the first time for 41 stars in the -2.74 <= [Fe/H] <= -0.56 metallicity range. The NLTE abundance corrections for Ag I 3382 A were found to be larger for the giants (up to 0.92~dex) than the dwarfs (up to 0.51~dex). In NLTE, Ag in our sample stars is enhanced relatively to Fe and the [Ag/Fe] Galactic trend is very similar to that for [Eu/Fe]; the [Ag/Eu], [Ag/Ba], and [Ag/Sr] abundance ratios of the r-II stars CS22892-052 and CS31082-001 agree very well with the r-process model of Prantzos et al. (2020); the -1.6 < [Fe/H] <= -0.56 stars have close-to-solar [Ag/Eu] ratios. We conclude that production of silver was dominated by the main r-process throughout the metallicity range we investigated, with the main s-process contribution of not larger than 20% for [Fe/H] > -1.6.
comments: 12 pages, four tables, seven figures; accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal

title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
authors: K. Abd El Dayem, N. Aimar, P. Amaro-Seoane, B. Aytaç, A. Berdeu, J.-P. Berger, G. Bourdarot, W. Brandner, Y. Cao, C. Correia, R. Davies, D. Defrère, A. Drescher, F. Eisenhauer, T. A. Ribeiro, S. Robbe-Dubois, M. Sadun Bordoni, J. Sánchez Bermúdez, J. Sauter, J. Scigliuto, J. Shangguan, T.T. Shimizu, J. Stadler, F. Soulez, C. Straubmeier, E. Sturm, M. Subroweit, C. Sykes, L.J. Tacconi, P. Thevenet, F. Thiel, V. Thoss, I. Urso, F. Vincent, S. von Fellenberg, J. Woillez, G. Zins
abstract: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

title: Atmospheric Parameter Determination of RR Lyrae Stars With Mephisto Multi-band Photometry
authors: Xingzhu Zou, Maosheng Xiang, Tanda Li, Lanya Mou, Haibo Yuan, Xinlei Chen, Yu Pan, Kaushik Chatterjee, Guowang Du, Yuan Fang, Helong Guo, Brajesh Kumar, Edoardo P. Lagioia, Chenxu Liu, Xiangkun Liu, Tao Wang, Yuan-Pei Yang, Jinghua Zhang, Shiyan Zhong, Xufeng Zhu, Xiaowei Liu
abstract: Phase-resolved atmospheric parameters of pulsating stars, including RR Lyrae stars and Cepheids, are essential for studying stellar structure and pulsation physics and for establishing accurate stellar benchmarks for Galactic structure and assembly history. We present a photometric framework that simultaneously infers Teff, log g, and [Fe/H] from Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band (u, v, g, r, i, z) photometry. A supervised neural-network forward model is built by training on synthetic colors derived from theoretical stellar atmosphere models. It reproduces the synthetic colors to a precision of 0.01 per cent. The model is applied to observed multi-epoch colors to derive phase-dependent atmospheric parameters. We apply the method to six RRab and four RRc stars in three globular clusters observed with Mephisto. We find typical per-phase uncertainties of about 62 K in effective temperature (Teff), 0.10 dex in surface gravity (log g), and 0.16 dex in metallicity ([Fe/H]). Repeated measurements across the pulsation cycle reduce the typical formal uncertainty of the final [Fe/H] estimates to roughly 0.03 dex. A sensitivity analysis indicates that the five Mephisto colors provide distinct and complementary constraints on the three stellar atmospheric parameters: (u-v) provides robust constraints on log g, (v-g) is informative for estimating [Fe/H], and (u-v), (v-g), (g-r), (r-i), and (i-z) all provide information on Teff. The results demonstrate that Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band photometry can deliver precise, cost-effective phase-resolved atmospheric parameters for RR Lyrae stars, offering an efficient way to construct large samples of stellar benchmarks for studies of stellar pulsation physics and Galactic structure and evolution.

figs.cap: Synthetic stellar loci in the $(g-i)$ versus $(u-v)$, $(v-g)$, $(g-r)$, $(r-i)$, and $(i-z)$ color planes. From top to bottom, the loci are coded according to values of $T_{\rm eff}$, $\log g$, and [Fe/H], respectively. The different color gradients illustrate the varying sensitivities of the Mephisto color combinations to the three basic atmospheric parameters.

Architecture of the adopted neural-network forward model. The atmospheric parameters ($T_{\rm eff}$, $\log g$, and [Fe/H]) are fed into two parallel branches: a parameter representation and a spectrum reconstruction branch. Their learned features are fused to predict the five Mephisto color indices. The network is trained with a joint loss consisting of the color prediction loss and the auxiliary spectrum reconstruction loss.

title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
authors: Hillary Davis, Joss Bland-Hawthorn, Thor Tepper-Garcia, Oscar Agertz, Elizabeth Iles
abstract: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four major spiral arms, including the Norma-Outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the "Norma arm" extending from one end of the Galaxy's central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. We now use a new generation of N-body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year old masers instead trace the Galactic bar's Quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust-lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the bar's parameters to be: a ~ 4.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, b ~ 2.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, phi = 20 (+5/-2) deg, Omega_p <~ 40 km s^-1 kpc^-1, representing the bar's semi-major and semi-minor half-lengths, inclination angle and pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way's spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

title: Kinematic methods of spiral nature identification: limitations and applicability
authors: Valeria S. Kostiuk, V. D. Zozulia, A. A. Marchuk, A. S. Gusev, I. V. Chugunov, A. A. Smirnova
abstract: The nature of spiral arms in galaxies remains debated, with several competing formation scenarios, including density waves, kinematic spirals, dynamic spirals, and recurrent modes, that are difficult to distinguish observationally. We tested two kinematic methods - the phase reversal method and the velocity harmonic dominance method - using toy models and mock data from TNG50 simulations. For bar resonances, the phase reversal method is strongly orientation-dependent and yields reliable corotation estimates only when the bar is aligned with the disc minor axis. For spiral arms, the phase reversal method does not always yield reliable results and should be used in tondem with another kinematic method. The velocity harmonic dominance method is more robust: it distinguishes between density wave, kinematic, and dynamic spiral patterns, although it still shows some sensitivity to orientation. Uncertainties in the rotation curve do not strongly affect its results. We also apply both methods to the observed grand-design spiral galaxy NGC3938 as an illustrative example; the results suggest the presence of multiple spiral modes, consistent with the recurrent modes scenario and this interpretation relies on different indirect evidence. Based on our findings, we propose a strategy for classifying spiral structure in observed galaxies that combines multiple independent tests. Applying this analysis to an extended sample will allow us to validate its predictive power and to investigate the diversity of spiral formation scenarios.
comments: 17 pages, 11 figures, accepted in MNRAS

title: J060242.22+332452.7: hierarchical triple system with inner eclipsing contact binary
authors: Mikhail Kovalev
abstract: I present a discovery of hierarchical triple system J060242.22+332452.7. Inner contact binary system shows clear eclipse timing variation (ETV) due to light time travel effect (LTTE), with LAMOST medium resolution spectra reveals radial velocity (RV) changes of the third star. Joint fit of ETV and RV allows determination of outer orbit with period $P_{\rm out}=1866\pm6$ days and $e_3=0.40\pm0.05$. The masses are $M_{\rm AB,~C}\sin^3{i_3}=2.02\pm0.22,~0.86\pm0.08~M_\odot$. This system is expected to have an astrometric orbit in the next data release of Gaia.
comments: submitted to AAS journals

title: Episodic Plasma Flows and Coronal Brightenings in an Arch Filament System Observed with SUNRISE III
authors: Sergio Javier González Manrique, Juan Carlos Trelles Arjona, Christoph Kuckein, Azaymi L. Siu-Tapia, Fernando Moreno-Insertis, Samrat Sen, Sami K. Solanki, Adur Pastor Yabar, Andrés Asensio Ramos, Daniel Nóbrega-Siverio, Manuel Collados, David Orozco Suárez, María Helena Rivero González, Sara Esteban Pozuelo, Jose Carlos del Toro Iniesta, Maria Balaguer Jiménez, Esteban Sanchis Kilders, Ignacio Torralbo, Yukio Katsukawa, Yusuke Kawabata, Hirohisa Hara, Toshifumi Shimizu, Takayoshi Oba, Andreas Lagg, Achim Gandorfer, Pietro Bernasconi, Thomas Berkefeld, Alex Feller, Tino L. Riethmüller, Alberto Álvarez-Herrero, Masahito Kubo, H. N. Smitha, Bianca Grauf, Michael Carpenter, Alexander Bell, Valentín Martínez Pillet, Francisco Javier Bailén, Julian Blanco Rodríguez, Juan Sebastián Castellanos Durán, Edvarda Harnes, Johannes Hoelken, Francisco A. Iglesias, Ryohtaroh T. Ishikawa, Takuma Matsumoto, Hanna Strecker, Dušan Vukadinović
abstract: Emerging flux regions (EFRs) transport magnetic flux and release energy in the solar atmosphere, often hosting arch filament systems (AFSs). We present high-resolution observations of an EFR obtained with Sunrise III, combining the Tunable Magnetograph (TuMag), the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared Spectro-Polarimeter (SCIP), and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). The dataset follows an AFS continuously for nearly four hours. Line-of-sight (LOS) velocities derived from the Mg I b$_2$ line reveal three episodic plasma-flow events, with downflows reaching approximately 17 km s$^{-1}$ at the footpoints and enhanced upflows near the loop tops. Although this pattern agrees with the classical emergence and draining scenario, the strongest upflows and downflows occur nearly simultaneously. Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) observations at 304 and 171 Angstrom reveal transient extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) brightenings in the surrounding emerging system. Some occur during enhanced-flow episodes, while others do not, indicating that the temporal correspondence is not systematic. Multiline spectropolarimetric inversions reveal temperatures between approximately 4000 and 10,000 K and a smooth variation of magnetic field inclination along a representative AFS loop. Non-force-free-field extrapolations provide the large-scale magnetic context of the low-lying AFS loops and surrounding coronal structures. Together, the observations reveal a spatially and temporally complex evolution without establishing a direct causal connection between local plasma-flow enhancements and EUV brightenings.
comments: 17 pages, 5 figures. Published in ApJL. Two animations are available with the online journal article

The horizontal and vertical axes in all panels correspond to helioprojective coordinates (arcsec) in the standard WCS reference frame. These observations provide the multi-instrument and multiline context of the AFS studied in this work. The five panels show the HMI line-of-sight magnetic field (top left), AIA 304 Å intensity (top center), HMI continuum intensity (top right), AIA 171 Å intensity (bottom left), and AIA 193 Å intensity (bottom center). The TuMag and SCIP fields of view marked in the static figure are not overplotted in the animation. The sequence shows the evolution of the photospheric magnetic concentrations and sunspots, changes in the morphology and brightness of the surrounding EUV loop structures, and transient EUV brightenings. The animation is available with the online journal article.

Line-of-sight velocity maps derived from the Mg I b$_{2}$ observations obtained with TuMag during the evolution of the arch filament system. Panels (a)–(d) show representative snapshots at four key stages of the event: (a) the beginning of the Sunrise III observing sequence (10:08 UT), (b) the onset of the filament eruption (11:23 UT), (c) the end of the eruption phase (11:50 UT), and (d) one of the strongest plasma-flow episodes around 12:11 UT. Physical parameters derived from the joint inversion of the Fe I 8468 Å and Ca II 8542 Å lines from SCIP using the DeSIRe inversion code. The top row shows the inferred temperature, magnetic field strength, and magnetic field inclination at log $\tau=-1$ (photosphere), while the middle row displays the same parameters at log $\tau=-5$ (chromosphere). title: Chemodynamical Study and Evidence for Hot Compact Companions to Blue Straggler Stars in Berkeley 31
authors: Deniz Cennet Çınar, D. Bisht, Ing-Guey Jiang, K. Belwal, Selçuk Bilir
abstract: We present a detailed study of the open cluster Berkeley 31 using Gaia DR3 astrometry, Gaia-ESO Survey DR5.1 spectroscopy, and multi-wavelength photometry. We identify 329 probable cluster members from their proper motions and trigonometric parallaxes and use them to examine the cluster's fundamental parameters, stellar populations, and Galactic orbit. The cluster is located at a distance of $6024 \pm 181$ pc, with a color excess of $E(B-V)=0.148 \pm 0.047$ mag, and has a mean metallicity of [Fe/H] $=-0.36 \pm 0.04$ dex and $\langle [\alpha/{\rm Fe}] \rangle=0.21 \pm 0.04$ dex. Isochrone fitting gives an age of $3.7 \pm 0.2$ Gyr, consistent with the independent chemical-clock estimate of $3.72 \pm 1.42$ Gyr. The systemic radial velocity is $57.89 \pm 0.08$ km s$^{-1}$. We find that about 38% of the MS stars are unresolved binary candidates with $q \gtrsim 0.5$. We identify 62 BSSs and 2 YSS candidates, including 48 BSSs and both YSSs not previously reported in the literature. We constructed multi-wavelength SEDs for these stars, including Swift/UVOT data for 28 BSSs. Two BSSs show clear ultraviolet excesses and are consistent with compact hot companions, one with a hot WD and the other with a pre-ELM WD. The present orbital parameters give a guiding radius of $12.29 \pm 0.29$ kpc and an eccentricity of $0.11 \pm 0.01$. Comparison with the estimated chemical birth radius indicates a moderate outward shift of the guiding center, with the present orbital position also contributing to the radial displacement. These results consistently describe Berkeley 31 as an intermediate-age, metal-poor outer-disk cluster and place its stellar populations in the context of its Galactic dynamical history.
comments: 27 pages, including 14 figures and 4 tables, accepted for publication in the The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)

title: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows
authors: Danat Issa, Ore Gottlieb, Jonatan Jacquemin-Ide, Matthew Liska
abstract: Black hole (BH) spin grows as accretion supplies angular momentum and decreases as magnetically driven jets remove it, driving the BH toward an equilibrium spin, $a_{\rm \star; eq}$. Existing estimates of $a_{\rm \star; eq}$ rely on general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations with fixed BH mass and spin, and cover only the extreme limits of horizon magnetic flux $\phi\rightarrow0$ and magnetically arrested disks (MADs), $\phi\approx\phi_{\rm MAD}$. We evolve the BH mass and spin in long 3D GRMHD simulations of radiatively inefficient accretion flows aligned or anti-aligned with the BH spin. We find the spin-up parameter as a function of BH spin and $\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}$, and derive the equilibrium spin as a continuous function of flux, $a_{\rm \star; eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD})$. The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm \star; eq}\approx0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm \star; eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx0.5$ to $a_{\rm \star; eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx0.06$ in sustained MADs. In weakly magnetized flows, a slowly spinning BH must accrete at least its initial mass to reach equilibrium, whereas MADs spin down rapidly rotating BHs after accreting less than half of it. However, as the BH grows, the growing gravitational radius and enhanced inflow reduce $\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}$, driving disks whose magnetic-flux supply cannot keep pace out of the MAD state and allowing the BH to transition from spin-down to spin-up. The final spin thus depends on both the magnetic flux history and the accreted mass. We discuss implications for a variety of BH-powered engines and provide a subgrid prescription for galaxy-scale simulations and population studies.

title: Testing Extended Exponential Infrared Teleparallel Gravity with CMB, DESI, and PantheonPlus
authors: Mahmoud Hashim, Jackson Levi Said, Waleed El Hanafy, Eleonora Di Valentino
abstract: We place cosmological constraints on an extended exponential infrared (EExpIR) $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model using current observational datasets. The extension is characterized by an additional parameter, $b$, which governs the late-time cosmological dynamics. Owing to the existence of two solution branches, phase-space analysis is employed to select the cosmological branch and to establish an appropriate prior range for the new parameter. In this framework, the torsion sector acts as an effective dark-energy component, exhibiting a smooth evolution from a quintessence-like phase to a phantom regime, while recovering the standard cosmological behavior at early times. To constrain the model parameters, we combine early-Universe observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT measurements of the CMB with late-time probes from DESI BAO and PantheonPlus Type Ia supernovae. Using the full dataset, including the SH0ES calibration, we obtain $b=0.573^{+0.016}_{-0.060}$ and $H_0=70.67^{+0.31}_{-0.35}~{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ at 68\% CL. Model comparison based on Bayesian evidence reveals that the EExpIR $f(T)$ and the $\Lambda$CDM models are statistically indistinguishable when only CMB data are considered, whereas the inclusion of the full cosmological dataset with SH0ES leads to a weak preference in favor of $\Lambda$CDM.

title: Infrared spectroscopy of the longest-period Galactic Mira variables from Palomar Gattini-IR: Identification of a candidate thermally pulsing Super-Asymptotic Giant Branch star
authors: Ming To Suen, Kishalay De, Sam Rose, Rajorshi Bhattacharya, Viraj Karambelkar, Michael C. B. Ashley, Cuc Dinh, Nicholas Earley, Danielle Frostig, Matthew Hankins, Charles D. Kilpatrick, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Anna M. Moore, Roberto Soria, Aswin Suresh, Tony Travouillon
abstract: The population of extremely long-period Mira variables in the Milky Way remains poorly characterized. Their rarity and heavy circumstellar obscuration have precluded systematic studies in optical surveys, yet they are expected to trace the most massive stars evolving through the Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB). We present IRTF/SpeX spectroscopy of the longest-period ($P\gtrsim1000$ d) Galactic Mira variables identified with the Palomar Gattini-IR survey. Twelve of thirteen targets exhibit characteristics consistent with massive O-rich AGB stars. In contrast, one peculiar source IRAS 19552+3142 exhibits i) a large-amplitude ($\Delta J\gtrsim2$ mag) pulsations with $P\approx1060$ d, ii) strong C$_2$ and CO molecular bands indicating C/O$\gtrsim1$, and iii) SiC emission at $\approx11.3\,\mu$m in archival mid-infrared spectra. Its spectroscopically confirmed chemistry makes it the longest period C-rich Galactic Mira variable known; together with the rarity of similar objects, this source is difficult to reconcile with standard massive AGB evolution where hot-bottom burning maintains an O-rich surface composition. Instead, its properties may be explained by super-AGB evolution where dredge-out episodes produce a C-rich surface and circumstellar material. Its high luminosity ($M_{[4.5]}\lesssim-10$ mag), red color ($[3.6] - [4.5]\gtrsim2.0$ mag), and high mass-loss rate ($\gtrsim 10^{-4} \mathrm{M_\odot yr^{-1}}$) resemble extreme AGB star progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients in nearby galaxies and a known chemically peculiar super-AGB star candidate in the Small Magellanic Cloud. IRAS 19552+3142 may thus provide a rare look at a Galactic super-AGB star in the thermally pulsing phase. Our results motivate improved theoretical predictions and long-baseline infrared searches for these short-lived, dust-enshrouded endpoints of stellar evolution.
comments: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to PASP. Comments welcome!

title: 2026 ED138: A Large Trans-Neptunian Object in Early Rubin Observatory Data, and How Many More May Remain
authors: Matthew J. Holman, Mario Jurić, Kevin J. Napier, Jacob A. Kurlander, Aren Heinze, Joachim Moeyens, Megan E. Schwamb, Pedro H. Bernardinelli, Ian Sullivan, Eric C. Bellm, Silvia Protopapa, Colin Orion Chandler, Ian Chow, Eric J. Christensen, Samuel Cornwall, Siegfried Eggl, Sarah Greenstreet, Chester Li, Erfan Nourbakhsh, James E. Robinson, Devanshi Singh, Danica Zilkova
abstract: We characterize a large trans-Neptunian object (TNO), 2026 ED138, discovered in data taken by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory with the linking code pointdexter, and validate it independently. 2026 ED138 has absolute magnitude $H_V=3.19$, implying a diameter of 612-1530 km for geometric albedos between 0.25 and 0.04 and making it one of the ten intrinsically brightest known TNOs and a dwarf-planet candidate. At $i\approx19.4$ it is bright enough in the sky for ground-based spectroscopy and light curves and for detailed study with HST and JWST. Archival DECam detections extend its arc to more than ten years (3789 days). Its orbit, with barycentric $a=43.09$ au, $e=0.139$ and $i=24.4^\circ$, lies at the edge of the 12:7 mean-motion resonance with Neptune, like that of the dwarf planet Haumea, but with $g-r=0.63$ it is too red to be a member of Haumea's collisional family. 2026 ED138 was missed by earlier surveys because it lies far south and near the crowded regions of the Galactic plane. Our recoveries of the known TNOs with $H_V<4$ suggest that about 3 more objects like them, and probably more, remain undiscovered away from the Galactic plane. More such objects probably lie within $10^\circ$ of the plane, which no search has yet covered to this depth.
comments: 30 pages, 9 figures, 12 tables. Submitted to AJ

title: On The Scaling Relations Between Black Holes And The Galaxy/Bulge Mass And Their Connections With The Black Hole Occupation Fraction
authors: Emanuele Contini, J.K. Jang, Jinsu Rhee, Changjo Seo, Sukyoung K. Yi
abstract: We investigate the black hole (BH)--host galaxy scaling relations predicted by the semianalytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, focusing on their dependence on BH mass threshold, galaxy morphology, and redshift, and on their connection with the BH occupation fraction (BHOF). Using the YS200 cosmological simulation as our reference volume, we study the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ and $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm bulge}$ relations for different BH mass selections and compare their redshift evolution with the hydrodynamical zoom-in simulation \texttt{NewCluster}. We find that BH mass cuts primarily affect the low-mass regime, while the selected relations progressively converge toward the intrinsic no-cut relations at higher host masses. The $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ relation also depends systematically on galaxy morphology, with increasingly bulge-dominated systems preferentially occupying higher stellar masses. Over $z=0$--$3$, FEGA25 shows no clear systematic evolution of either scaling relation, consistent with a broadly preserved statistical connection between BH and host-galaxy growth. NewCluster shows no clear monotonic evolution either, although it exhibits larger scatter, particularly toward high host masses. We further show that BHOF and BH--host scaling relations encode complementary information. A low BHOF generally corresponds to a stronger selection-induced offset, but the mapping is not unique: substantially different occupation fractions can yield similar median scaling relations, and at fixed BHOF the bias depends on the host property and underlying BH mass distribution. At $z=0$, \texttt{FEGA25} is consistent with available observational constraints for both stellar- and bulge-mass relations, while predicting increased scatter and bending toward lower host masses.
comments: 17 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ApJ, comments welcome!

The upper panels show $M_{\rm BH}$ as a function of total stellar mass (left) and bulge stellar mass (right), while the lower panels show the corresponding black hole occupation fractions, $f_{\rm BH,occ}$. Blue circles and orange squares refer to the selections $M_{\rm BH}>10^{5}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ and $M_{\rm BH}>10^{6}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, respectively, while the black curves in the upper panels show the no-cut relations. The vertical dashed lines mark the host masses at which $f_{\rm BH,occ}=0.5$, determined by interpolation between adjacent mass bins. For the stellar-mass relation, these occur at $\log(M_{\star,50}/{\rm M}_{\odot})\simeq 8.30$ and $9.19$ for the $10^{5}$ and $10^{6}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ thresholds, respectively. For the bulge-mass relation, the $10^{6}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ threshold reaches $f_{\rm BH,occ}=0.5$ at $\log(M_{{\rm bulge},50}/{\rm M}_{\odot})\simeq 7.88$, whereas the occupation fraction for $M_{\rm BH}>10^{5}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ is already above 0.5 at the lower edge of the plotted bulge-mass range. The figure shows that large differences in occupation fraction do not necessarily translate into equally large differences in the corresponding median scaling relations, highlighting the complementary information carried by black hole demographics and black hole–host scaling relations.

The vertical axis is defined as $\Delta_{\rm sel}={\rm median}(\log M_{\rm BH})_{\rm cut}-{\rm median}(\log M_{\rm BH})_{\rm no\,cut}$ and therefore quantifies, in each host-mass bin, the upward shift of the median scaling relation induced by the adopted black hole mass threshold. Blue and orange curves correspond to $M_{\rm BH}>10^{5}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ and $M_{\rm BH}>10^{6}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, respectively. Solid curves with open circles show the results obtained when binning galaxies by total stellar mass, while dashed curves with open diamonds refer to bulge stellar mass. The vertical dashed line marks $f_{\rm BH,occ}=0.5$, and the horizontal dashed line indicates $\Delta_{\rm sel}=0$. Large values of $\Delta_{\rm sel}$ are preferentially associated with low occupation fractions, where the black hole mass cut selects only the high-$M_{\rm BH}$ tail of the underlying population. As $f_{\rm BH,occ}$ approaches unity, the selected and no-cut median relations progressively converge and $\Delta_{\rm sel}$ approaches zero. At fixed $f_{\rm BH,occ}$, however, the offset can differ substantially between the stellar-mass and bulge-mass relations, showing that the occupation fraction alone does not uniquely determine the selection bias and that its impact also depends on the host property used to define the scaling relation.
