title: Analysis of Multi-Wavelength Data for 30 Galactic Emission-Line Stars with Dusty Envelopes
authors: A.Zh.Naurzbayeva, A.S.Miroshnichenko, N.Sh.Alimgazinova, S.V.Zharikov, C.Rossi, I.V.Reva, R.I.Kokumbayeva, Ch.T.Omarov, A.Raj, M.S.Bisht, A.Joshi, A.K.Kuratova, R.J.Rudy, R.C.Puetter, R.B.Perry, N.Manset, N.L.Vaidman, Sh.T.Nurmakhametova, A.B.Manapbayeva, S.A.Khokhlov
abstract: We selected 30 stars with V-band brightnesses of 11-16 mag, visual color-indices B-V of approximately 1.3 mag or less, and large near-IR color-indices (J-H and H-K of approximately 0.7 mag or greater) to search for the presence of the B[e] phenomenon. Spectroscopic observations confirmed the presence of emission lines previously detected in 11 stars of the sample and revealed them in 4 other stars for the first time. Spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in the optical and IR spectral regions were analyzed and compared with theoretical SEDs. The fundamental parameters were estimated using the SED fits corrected for the interstellar and circumstellar (CS) extinction and Gaia DR3 distance measurements. Properties of 14 objects previously classified as pre-main-sequence stars were reevaluated. The B[e] phenomenon was found in 16 objects, most of which exhibit observed properties of FS CMa type objects, a still small group of Galactic stars or binary systems with predominantly hot CS dust. Properties of 2 objects (IRAS 06237+0020 and IRAS 19156-0935) are consistent with those of Proto-Planetary Nebulae at early phases of this evolutionary stage. The nature and evolutionary status of 11 sample objects remain uncertain and require further investigation.
comments: 21 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables

title: Identifying narrow-band mutual coupling resonances in SKA-low stations using frequency-independent current basis functions
authors: John Cumner, Oscar S.D. O'Hara, Quentin Gueuning, Anthony Brown, Fred Dulwich, Oskar Zetterstrom
abstract: Mutual coupling between closely spaced elements in aperture arrays introduces narrow-band spectral features in the Embedded Element Patterns (EEPs), threatening measurements of the 21-cm power spectrum with instruments such as SKA-low. We detail a method to identify such features through the construction of frequency-independent current basis functions, utilising a singular value decomposition of frequency-dependent basis functions. We demonstrate the method on a three-element linear array and full pseudo-random station of SKA log-periodic antennas and examine the current power induced by mutual coupling. For the pseudo-random layout station we note many narrow-band resonance features, including strong resonances at 50.8~MHz and 83.6~MHz, where the coupled power on the passive antennas can approach or exceed that of the excited antenna. Simulated delay power spectra for the SKA-low core show that observing in frequency bands including resonance features causes large foreground leakage within the delay power spectra, obscuring the EoR window. For the pseudo-random layout station with SKALA4.0 we identify two significant frequency bands from 59.2--76.2~MHz and 84.2--103.3~MHz which are free of contamination from current resonances, preserving the EoR window in these frequency ranges.

title: Four-hundred Very Metal-poor Stars Studied with LAMOST and Subaru. IV. Heavy Element Enhanced Stars
authors: Yangming Lin, Haining Li, Wako Aoki, Ruizheng Jiang, Tadafumi Matsuno, Zhenyu He, Ruizhi Zhang, Zhuohan Li, Satoshi Honda, Gang Zhao
abstract: We perform a homogeneous analysis of 82 heavy-element-enhanced metal-poor stars from the\\ LAMOST/Subaru sample, including 64 $r$-process-enhanced stars, 2 limited-$r$ stars, and 16 stars exhibiting significant or moderate carbon enhancement (comprising 9 $s$-process-enhanced, 2 $r$-process-enhanced, 2 $r$/$s$, and 3 $r$+$s$ stars). Systematic differences in $\mathrm{[X/Eu]}$ between $r$-I and $r$-II stars, together with their distinct dynamical properties, suggest that $r$-II stars likely formed in low-mass dwarf galaxies where contamination from additional nucleosynthetic channels was minimal. We have also discovered a number of peculiar objects. We identify an extremely metal-poor $r$-II star, J1158+0734 ($\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$ = -2.93), whose enhanced Zn abundance ($\mathrm{[Zn/Fe]}$ = +0.67) is best explained by yields from a high-energy, massive core-collapse supernova. The surface abundances of $s$-process-enhanced stars exhibit pronounced dispersion, consistent with enrichment from AGB progenitors with diverse properties. Notably, one star, J2256+0215, reveals compelling evidence for additional evolutionary mixing, as indicated by its unusually low carbon abundance ($\mathrm{[C/Fe]}$ = +0.08) and extremely low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 2.33. Additionally, we identify 3 $r$+$s$ stars whose abundance patterns reveal combined contributions from both the $r$- and $s$-processes. We further propose a modified diagnostic scheme for the identification of CEMP-$r$+$s$ stars, defined as: -0.2 $\leqslant$ $\mathrm{[La/Nd]}$ $\leqslant$ 0.2 and -0.5 $\leqslant$ $\mathrm{[Eu/Nd]}$ $\leqslant$ 0.0.
comments: 26 pages, published in The Astrophysical Journal

title: Nine new eclipsing accreting ultracompact white dwarf binaries from the Zwicky Transient Facility
authors: J. van Roestel, M. J. Green, T. L. S. Wong, P. Szkody, J. M. Khalil, A. Householder, K. B. Burdge, T. A. Prince, L. Blomberg, I. Caiazzo, K. K. Das, N. Yamaguchi, A. C. Rodriguez, Z. P. Vanderbosch, E. C. Bellm, T. X. Chen, A. J. Drake, M. J. Graham, G. Helou, M. M. Kasliwal, R. L. Riddle, B. Rusholme
abstract: Accreting ultracompact white dwarf binaries (accreting UCBs) transfer helium-rich material at orbital periods below about 65 min, and mainly divide into hydrogen-free AM CVn binaries and helium cataclysmic variables. Eclipsing systems are of particular value: they allow the component masses and radii to be measured independently of any model, the most direct test of the proposed formation channels, and they form a sample with a simple, well-understood selection function. Only 21 eclipsing accreting white dwarf UCBs have been published. We aim to enlarge the sample of eclipsing accreting UCBs available for detailed characterisation. We searched the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) light curves of Gaia-selected candidates and of ZTF-selected dwarf novae for short-period eclipse signals using a box least-squares period search. Identification spectra of nine systems were obtained with LRIS on the Keck I telescope. We present nine new discoveries and re-analyse the four systems first reported by Khalil et al. (2024). Eclipses are detected directly in the survey photometry of all 13 systems, which have orbital periods between 26.0 and 65.0 min and median ZTF magnitudes $g = 18.7-21.5$. Ten are consistent with being AM CVn binaries, and two are likely helium cataclysmic variables (of which one may host a high-state disc). The remaining system, ZTF J2116+2446, shows only hydrogen lines, making it the shortest-period UCB with hydrogen but no detected helium; it may have evolved from a white dwarf-brown dwarf binary. The nine new systems increase the number of published eclipsing accreting UCBs from 21 to 30. Because they are eclipsing, they are immediately available for the high-speed photometric modelling that yields model-independent masses and radii, to be presented in future work, including for the three hydrogen-rich systems that are key tests of the evolved cataclysmic-variable channel.
comments: to be submitted to A and A, comments welcome

title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
authors: Anastasios Avgoustidis, Edmund J. Copeland, Adam Moss, Juhan Raidal, Filippo Revello, Gonzalo Villa
abstract: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their Gravitational Wave (GW) contributions as well as their impact on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Performing an MCMC analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the GW emission at frequencies between the current PTA and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. However, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the GW data as well as other favoured models.
comments: 31 pages, 17 figures

title: SDSS-V LVM: Mapping of plasma temperatures in the Lagoon Nebula reveals the origin of long-standing chemical abundance discrepancies
authors: Amrita Singh, Guillermo A. Blanc, Kathryn Kreckel, J. E. Méndez-Delgado, Christophe Morisset, Sebastián F. Sánchez, Oleg Egorov, Niv Drory, Nimisha Kumari, Fu-Heng Liang, Enrico Congiu, Alfredo Mejía-Narváez, Evelyn J. Johnston, José G. Fernández-Trincado, Hemanth Bommireddy, Abhinna Sundar Samantaray, Thomas Hilder, Rodolfo de J. Zermeño, Ivan Katkov, Dhanesh Krishnarao, Juna A. Kollmeier
abstract: Knowing the chemical composition of interstellar gas is essential for understanding the chemical evolution of galaxies. Ionized nebulae provide key laboratories for this purpose, where chemical abundances are commonly derived from emission lines of heavy ions such as doubly ionized oxygen, $O^{++}$. Abundances can be inferred either from collisionally excited lines (CELs) or from recombination lines (RLs). However, for more than 80 years, the former have yielded systematically lower abundances than the latter. We map this ''abundance discrepancy'' using the first spatially resolved integral field unit (IFU) observations of $O^{++}$ RLs and CELs across a Milky Way H II region: the Lagoon Nebula (a.k.a. M8). Modeling the data using a plasma temperature perturbation model, we present unequivocal evidence that electron temperature ($T_e$) fluctuations drive the abundance discrepancy in M8. We find a tight correlation between the abundance discrepancy and the difference between $T_e$ derived from the classical CEL method and a hybrid RL/CEL approach. We identify this Te discrepancy as an observational proxy for the amplitude of the thermal fluctuations, providing a new, direct way to quantify their effect on nebular abundances. The correlation constrains the mean electron temperature of the gas. Adopting this mean temperature reconciles CEL and RL abundances, effectively eliminating the abundance discrepancy.
comments: Accepted to ApJ. 12 pages, 6 Figures

The gray box represents a zoom-in region satisfying the $S/N>3$ for $\lambda 4363$, the subsequent diagnostic maps are shown within this gray box in Section IV.

title: Can the $\sim 5$ kpc starburst ring in MW create eROSITA bubbles?
authors: Mukesh Singh Bisht, Kartick C. Sarkar
abstract: eROSITA bubbles (eRBs) in our Galaxy are thought to be due to the energy injection by the central star-forming region or the central Super Massive Black Hole. Identifying the origin of these bubbles is crucial in constraining the origin of the Fermi Bubbles and the nature of the Galactic feedback. However, some recent opinions suggest that the eRBs may not even have been produced by any central source, but rather a result of a star-formation ring at $R\sim 5$ kpc. In this letter, we perform detailed hydrodynamic simulations to refute that claim and show that such a ring of star formation alone is not able to produce the symmetric eROSITA bubbles - one needs a compact energy injection from the Galactic Center to produce these bubbles. Our study, therefore, suggests that the eROSITA bubbles truly represent the nuclear outflow from our Galaxy.
comments: 7 pages, 3 figures, Submitted to ApJ

figs.cap: Temperature maps of the ’DI’ simulation (without the central energy injection). Top Panel: face on view at $17$, $33$, and $50$ Myr at $z=2$ kpc. With time (left to right), a larger number of star clusters are generated, resulting in hot (red) bubbles. A ring-like structure is seen around $\approx 5$ kpc, which corresponds to the peak in the SFR as shown in Fig.1 in the supplementary material. Bottom Panel: edge on view at $17$, $33$, and $50$ Myr at $Y=0$ kpc. Two horn-like chimneys rising from $X\sim 5$ kpc correspond to the overlapping hot bubbles from individual star clusters.
Same as Figure 1, but for the distributed + central injection (DI+CI) case.

X-ray surface brightness maps of two scenarios of star formation in the MW. One, without the presence of the central energy injection (left panel), and second, with the presence of a central energy injection corresponding to an SFR $=0.5$ M$_{⊙}$ yr$^{-1}$ (right panel). The absence of an eROSITA bubble in the first case clearly showcases that the $\sim 5$ kpc star formation ring in the MW is not able to produce the eRBs, and a central injection is necessary.

title: KM3-230213A: The Highest-Energy Cosmic Neutrino
authors: Carla Distefano
abstract: High-energy neutrinos provide a unique probe of the most extreme non-thermal processes in the Universe. The detection of the ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A by the KM3NeT neutrino telescope, with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV), represents a major step forward in neutrino astronomy. In this review, we summarize the main properties of the event and discuss its interpretation within different astrophysical and cosmological scenarios, including active galactic nuclei, transient sources, and cosmogenic neutrinos, highlighting the role of multi-messenger constraints. Despite extensive follow-up observations, no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been identified, and the event remains in tension with the absence of comparable detections in other experiments. This situation leaves open the possibility of more complex source scenarios or contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model. We also discuss the implications for the ultra-high-energy neutrino landscape and the prospects for future observations with next-generation detectors. KM3-230213A provides a unique opportunity to probe particle acceleration and neutrino production at energies far beyond the reach of terrestrial experiments.
comments: 24 pages, 13 figures, 1 table. Published in Physics and the Cosmos (2026)

The vertical dashed line indicates the observed value for KM3-230213A. Right: Reconstruction of the muon energy as a function of the number of triggered PMTs. The shaded bands represent the 68% confidence level intervals including statistical uncertainties only (dark blue) and statistical plus systematic uncertainties (light blue). The shaded region shows the effect of a $\pm 1.5^{\circ}$ variation in the reconstructed zenith angle, corresponding to the 68% systematic uncertainty. title: Extracting non-Gaussian information of line-intensity maps with weighted skew spectra
authors: Eleonora Vanzan, Azadeh Moradinezhad Dizgah, Ely D. Kovetz
abstract: The bispectrum of line-intensity maps carries cosmological and astrophysical information beyond the power spectrum, but its large data vector hampers the analysis of survey data. Skew spectra address this by compressing the bispectrum into a handful of power-spectrum-like observables, cross-spectra of the observed field with filtered squares of it. We present the first application of optimally weighted skew spectra to line-intensity mapping of galaxy-hosted emission, where all clustering and shot-noise terms are luminosity weighted and the mean intensity is unknown. We perform idealized real-space Fisher forecasts for a SPHEREx-like survey of H$\alpha$ emission at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 4.6$, in its deep fields and in a noisier all-sky configuration. First, the compression carries over to intensity maps: on perturbative scales and for a fixed redshift evolution of the emitters, four skew spectra, one of them matched to the shot noise, recover the bispectrum constraints on biases, shot noise and cosmological parameters to within a few percent. Second, the joint analysis of the power spectrum and the skew spectra measures the ratios of the second-order biases to the linear bias in each redshift bin. Within a bin the biases are degenerate with the unknown mean intensity, but their ratios are not, so their redshift evolution is measured without a model for the emitters. For emission that depends on halo mass alone, these ratios are determined by luminosity-weighted averages of the halo biases, so their evolution can test the halo-emission connection, including dependence on assembly history or environment. The bias ratios are not accessible to the tree-level real-space power spectrum alone. At $z \lesssim 3$ an all-sky SPHEREx-like configuration can detect departures of order $0.1$ in the bias ratios at $3\sigma$, while deeper fields perform better in the highest-redshift bins.

The lower panels show the ratio of the $\alpha$ response to the $b_{1}$ response, $(\partial\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}_{n},\delta_{\rm obs}}/\partial\alpha)/(\partial\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{S}_{n},\delta_{\rm obs}}/\partial b_{1})$, as a function of $k$, with the $\mathcal{L}_{0}$ ratio repeated in each panel as a reference (light curve). title: At the EDGES of MADness: phenomenology of relic millicharged atomic dark matter
authors: Eleonora Vanzan, Kimberly K. Boddy, Ely D. Kovetz
abstract: Millicharged dark matter lives in a corner of parameter space that has been considerably shrinking over the past decades, due to constraints from cosmology, astrophysical systems, and ground-based experiments. A particularly interesting probe is the 21-cm absorption signal at Cosmic Dawn, which attracted interest in light of the EDGES claim: the reported excess absorption can be explained by millicharged dark matter with a fractional electric charge of~$10^{-6} \lesssim \epsilon \lesssim 10^{-4}$, but it must be a subpercent of the total dark matter abundance to remain consistent with the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We show that very low fractions of millicharged dark matter naturally arise from atomic dark matter: a dark sector model that replicates the physics of standard atomic hydrogen. Dark ions undergo the process of dark recombination, leaving a relic ionized component that, in the presence of kinetic mixing, is naturally millicharged. We modify the cosmological Boltzmann solver CLASS to incorporate this scenario, and we investigate the parameter space of millicharged atomic dark matter (MAD) that is allowed by CMB, large-scale structure, and supernovae data. We find there are cosmologically viable regions of MAD parameter space that are consistent with laboratory and astrophysical bounds and also overlap with the EDGES-defined window. Although the EDGES result is likely not a Cosmic Dawn signal, MAD leaves distinctive cosmological signatures, accessible to upcoming 21-cm observations.

figs.cap: CMB temperature angular power spectrum (upper row) and present-day linear matter power spectrum (bottom row) for our three benchmark scenarios: SM-like (left), early dark recombination (middle), and late dark recombination (right). The values of the millicharge are chosen so that, in all three scenarios, they correspond to similar ratios of DM-SM to DM-DR interactions at the moment of dark decoupling ($\mathcal{R}\sim 10^{-4}-10^{-3}$, the parameter $\mathcal{R}$ is introduced in Sec. IV). The largest cross sections (those for $e_{D}-e$ scatterings) are of order $2\times 10^{-32}\,{\rm cm}^{2}$ in the SM-like case, $8\times 10^{-27}\,{\rm cm}^{2}$ in the early dark recombination case, and $10^{-33}\,{\rm cm}^{2}$ in the late dark recombination case.

The values of the cross sections in the three scenarios yield similar values of $\mathcal{R}\sim 10^{-3}$ in all three cases (compare the orange solid line to the solid blue line). Orange and blue: MAD with the same millicharge values as in Figure 2 (orange for the baryons, blue for the dark baryons). The MAD realization in the two leftmost columns corresponds to interaction cross sections already ruled out by Planck; the right column is the regime of interest for late-time probes.

Likelihood: Planck + ACT lensing + BAO + Pantheon Plus.

title: Seven Years of TESS Precovery Observations of the Dwarf-planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
authors: Te Han, Jeroen Audenaert, Daniel Muthukrishna, Matthew Holman, George R. Ricker
abstract: The trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED$_{138}$ was announced in 2026 October as the first dwarf-planet candidate in our solar system discovered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observed it in five month-long sectors between 2019 and 2026, four of them before its discovery. We subtract every Gaia DR3 star from these crowded full-frame images with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve (TGLC) package, then remove static residuals with a running median. Stacking the images along its predicted path detects 2026 ED$_{138}$ in all five sectors at 5-21$\sigma$, and at 34$\sigma$ combined. The TESS positions alone confirm the JPL orbit, and its brightness is consistent with the 0.08 mag fading expected from its increasing distance and changing phase angle.
comments: 4 pages, 1 figure

figs.cap: Top: TESS images ($19\times 19$ pixels, $6.5^{\prime}$) stacked along the path of 2026 ED$_{138}$ after subtracting all Gaia DR3 stars and static residuals, per sector and all sectors combined (red), on one color scale, with the significance in units of the control-track scatter $\sigma$. Middle: the sky path of 2026 ED$_{138}$ seen from TESS (JPL orbit), each sector’s segment, and the orbital elements from JPL and from TESS alone. Bottom: TESS magnitudes, with JPL’s prediction (thin line) and its value at opposition, when TESS observes (thick line). Scattered light may explain the fainter magnitude and lower precision of Sector 39.

title: The dark surface of (163693) Atira and implications for inner-Earth asteroid origins
authors: Bryce T. Bolin, Carl Ingebretsen, Robert Jedicke, William F. Bottke, Colin Orion Chandler, Rogerio Deienno, Alessandro Morbidelli, David Nesvorný, Leo Y. Alcorn, Percy Gomez, Meredith A. MacGregor
abstract: We compare the physical properties of inner-Earth asteroid (163693) Atira with the NEOMOD3 population model. Its radar-derived diameter of 4.9 km and absolute magnitude H$_V\simeq$16.4 imply a geometric albedo of p$_V\sim$0.02. Photometry with the Astrophysical Research Consortium 3.5-m telescope and ARCTIC yields g-r=0.49$\pm$0.03, r-i=0.20$\pm$0.02, i-z=0.02$\pm$0.03, a$^\ast$=$-0.05\pm0.03$, and a g-to-i spectral slope of 3.4$\pm$0.9$\%$/100 nm. The photometric reflectance favors a provisional X-type classification; combined with the low albedo, it supports a Tholen P-type interpretation. NEOMOD3 assigns an approximately 66$\%$ probability of delivery through inner Main Belt channels and 26$\%$ to central and outer Main Belt channels. Atira's NEOMOD3 albedo-category probabilities are $0.07\pm0.02$, $0.64\pm0.04$, and $0.29\pm0.04$ for p$_V<$0.1, 0.1$\leq$p$_V<$0.3, and p$_V\geq$0.3, respectively. Across 38 inner-Earth objects, including Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim, inner Main Belt delivery generally dominates, and intermediate albedo is favored for 33 objects. Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.
comments: 12 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AJ

[33] and Jurić et al. [36]. The mean a$^{∗}$ and $i$-$z$ C-, S-, and V-type asteroids are overplotted with one standard deviation error bars computed from the spectra of DeMeo et al. [21]. The location of the Sun at a$^{∗}$ = -0.13 and i-z = 0.03 is plotted with a large black-bordered yellow dot.

Vertical dashed lines indicate the effective wavelengths of the filters, with the data points offset slightly in wavelength for clarity. Error bars represent 1$\sigma$ uncertainties. The reflectance is normalized to unity at 550 nm, indicated by the red X. Shaded regions show the spectral ranges of X-type (blue), S-type (orange), and C-type (gray) asteroids from the Bus-DeMeo taxonomic catalog [21]. Among the templates shown, the X-type spectrum most closely matches Atira’s measured reflectance.

title: What kinds of strong star--black-hole encounters in AGN disks occur, and how often?
authors: R. O'Shaughnessy, Z. Rosenberg, J. Nordhaus
abstract: Disks surrounding active galactic nuclei contain many stars and black holes, which will inevitably encounter one another. The outcome of these encounters depends on how closely and how rapidly the bodies meet. Extending previous studies, we account for initial relative velocities seeded by stochastic effects in the disk; incorporate a strong-encounter cross-section accounting for single- and binary-mediated interactions computed via direct two-body (Hill) or three-body (isolated) interactions; and present a repeated-encounter model accounting both for energy loss due to stellar encounters as well as the SMBH tidal field. We convolve our encounter model with a parametric family of natal stellar and binary populations, focused on varying binary fraction and period distribution. In our fiducial disk model, even though single-single interactions supply most encounters, binary-mediated interactions supply 68% of collisions; most encounters are well-approximated as parabolic; and stochastically-driven relative velocities are comparatively substantial and driven by gravitational perturbations from disk fluctuations and neighboring bodies. Our tools are ready to use in downstream applications, including several easily-expressed semianalytic approximations to key interaction phenomena.
comments: 34 pages, plus 9-page supplemental material

figs.cap: Calibrated binary–single surface speeds. The cumulative rate-weighted distribution of the absolute signed-energy diagnostic $\zeta_{\star}$ at first contact. The vertical line marks $|\zeta_{\star}|=0.1$; $81.3$% of contacts lie below it. The Gaussian orbital average and RMS control use the same original population draws. Intervals describe sampling of resolved first contacts. See Appendix A.4 for more information. Produced by binary_analysis.py. Generated with LLM assistance per Appendix F.

The three channels deposit encounters in different places. Rate-weighted marginals of the stacked differential rate in the mass ratio $q$ (left), the scaled pericenter $x$ (center) and the scaled speed $u$ (right), per channel and summed. The mass-ratio marginals reflect the adopted stellar and BH mass functions together with each channel’s rate weighting. The pericenter marginal separates the channels completely: the shear channel peaks two decades outside the star while the resonant channels peak inside it, so only $0.336$ per cent of the former and $14.1$ per cent of the latter reach $x\leq 1$. The velocity marginal is confined to $u\leq 0.119$ at the $95$th percentile. The spike at $u=0$ is the bookkeeping bin for bound single–single samples and non-ionizing binary-mediated contributions (Sec. II.1 and Appendix A). It does not imply zero speed during a stellar passage or establish that each orbit is exactly parabolic. The right panel uses an approximation described in Appendix C. title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in SCAO systems: The Soft-Limiter approach
authors: Guido Agapito, Jueqi Lin, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Giulia Carlà, Enrico Pinna, Fabio Rossi
abstract: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von Kármán priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $\lambda_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$\lambda_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.
comments: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. 13 pages, 9 figures

figs.cap: Steady-state equilibria of the petal update (Eq. 10) for a physical step $\Delta P=600$ nm ($3\lambda_{WFS}/4$) at $0.8^{\prime\prime}$ seeing ($g_{\mathrm{eff}}=0.2285$, $\lambda_{WFS}=800$ nm). (a) Sensor restoring term $R(\Delta P-p)=R_{\mathrm{max}}\sin[2\pi(\Delta P-p)/\lambda_{WFS}]$, with $R_{\mathrm{max}}=g_{\mathrm{eff}}\lambda_{WFS}/2\pi$ (black; dashed lines at $\pm R_{\mathrm{max}}$), periodic in $\lambda_{WFS}$ (double arrow). The leak is drawn as the drain $g\,p$ subtracted at each frame, for $g=0$ (classical), $g=0.05$ (nominal) and $g=0.15$; the equilibria (zero net update) are its crossings with the sensor term, stable where the sensor term crosses the drain from above. The vertical gap between the two curves is the net update: shading shows its sign for the nominal gain (light blue: $p$ increases; grey: $p$ decreases). The dash-dotted line $g^{*}p$, with $g^{*}=g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$, passes through the sensor maximum at $p=\lambda_{WFS}/2$: above $g^{*}$ no command beyond half a fringe can be sustained. (b) Corresponding washboard potential $V(p)$ (Eq. 11; from bottom to top $g=0$, $0.05$, $0.15$, curves offset vertically): stable equilibria are valleys, unstable ones hills, and arrows show the direction of the update between them. Without leak all fringe wells are equally deep; the leak acts as a spring anchored at $p=0$, raising the distant wells until they disappear. At the nominal $g=0.05$ two stable states coexist ($p\approx 480$ nm and $p\approx-165$ nm); a step applied with the command at $p=0$ (square) falls in the basin of attraction of the wrapped state, as observed in Fig. 9. In the limit $\eta_{p}\to 0$ the washboard flattens: $V(p)$ reduces to a flat line for $g=0$ (the neutral random walk of Eq. 4) and to the single well $\frac{1}{2}gp^{2}$ for $g>0$, which keeps the loop bounded but retains no physical step.

Static estimation performance. The x-axis represents the differential piston $\Delta P_{i}=a_{i}-a_{\text{ref}}$ in nm. The plot compares the input $\Delta P$ distribution (blue) and the estimation error after MMSE subspace extraction (orange) over independent phase screens. The input mixture contains turbulence, random petals, and ELT M1/M2 wind-shake, demonstrating the estimator robustness to non-Kolmogorov low-order disturbances.

MMSE Subspace Extraction for a single static realization: (a) Accumulated total wavefront; (b) Injected ground-truth differential piston; (c) MMSE-estimated differential piston; (d) Estimation error. The RMS error for this specific realization is $157.4\,\mathrm{nm}$.

Closed-loop temporal stabilization and phase wrapping analysis. (a) Mean fringe-jump rate over 29 seconds. The EAC does not actively control petal modes, so its transitions reflect atmospheric wandering rather than actual control lock-ins. (b) Science-band petal error $\sigma_{P}(\lambda_{sci}=2200\penalty\ \mathrm{nm})$. The MMSE Soft-Limiter significantly outperforms the Classical integrator under severe turbulence without incurring the steady-state performance penalty of the EAC. (c) Fraction of seeds permanently locked in the correct fringe basin for the Classical integrator at good seeing (evaluated over 5 independent atmospheric and noise realizations).

Parametric scan of the Soft-Limiter leakage gain $g$. (a) K-band Strehl Ratio. (b) Petal residual RMS ($\|\Delta P\|/\sqrt{5}$). Open rings indicate the nominal operating point selected for each seeing condition. The shaded band in (b) represents the theoretical threshold range $g\lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$ plotted for $0.6^{\prime\prime}$ and $0.8^{\prime\prime}$ seeing (where the retention condition is satisfied), while the vertical dotted lines mark the nominal retention threshold $g^{*}=g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$ for each corresponding seeing, and the horizontal line marks the capture-range limit $\lambda_{WFS}/4=200\,\mathrm{nm}$, beyond which the sinusoidal sensor response is no longer monotonic. Crossing this line while descending in $g$ marks the onset of the divergence described in the text; the rise of all curves as $g\to 1$ has a different origin, the loop no longer accumulating any petal correction at all. The optimum is strongly asymmetric: underestimating $g$ under severe turbulence leads to a large loss of Strehl.

Dynamic response to a severe $0\to 600\,\mathrm{nm}$ physical step at $0.8^{\prime\prime}$ seeing ($g=0.05$). Left: Because the step is injected from an initial command $p=0$, which lies in the basin of attraction of the wrapped well (Fig. 3), the loop settles one fringe away. The command stably retains the fractional state at $\approx-164\,\mathrm{nm}$ (with a $\approx 36\,\mathrm{nm}$ droop), leaving a residual of $\approx 764\,\mathrm{nm}$ uncorrected. Right: The corresponding K-band Strehl Ratio drops to $\approx 0.2$ for the entire duration of the $600\,\mathrm{nm}$ step due to the uncorrected integer fringe. This demonstrates the fast loop stably holding the fractional state, leaving the integer ambiguity to be resolved by the slow phasing sensor.

title: Model-Based Retrieval of Four Years of JWST/NIRCam Wavefronts
authors: Shrishmoy Ray, Benjamin Pope, Louis Desdoigts, Hayden Greer, Milo Langker, Peter Tuthill, Marshall Perrin, Anand Sivaramakrishnan, Alexandra Greenbaum, Laurent Pueyo, Max Charles
abstract: The fidelity of data recovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) depends on precise monitoring of the mirror segments' surfaces and alignment. To this end, every few days the observatory takes pairs of defocused images of a reference star with its NIRCam instrument; a closed-source phase retrieval package is then employed to infer the wavefront. We here present camino (Computational Aberration Modelling and Inference for NIRCam Observations), an open-source algorithm to model NIRCam built in JAX using the differentiable Fresnel optics code dLUX and regularised maximum likelihood inference that has been conditioned on the entire archive of NIRCam wavefront sensing data. We typically improve the reduced chi-squared in fits to the defocused data from 60-65 to 12-13. We reconstruct the wavefront history of JWST from the beginning of science operations to early 2026. This open source implementation operates in parallel to the current STScI phase retrieval algorithm, allowing access by the broader scientific community to high-accuracy wavefront estimation and enabling its direct integration into science-analysis workflows. This represents a major step towards the ultimate goal of predictive calibration methods based on physics-based forward modelling, obviating the need for time-consuming observation of contemporaneous dedicated reference stars.
comments: 13 pages, 9 figures, Submitted to PASA

title: Theoretical Consistency and Observational Constraints on Entropic Cosmology
authors: Yunliang Ren, Xiaofeng Yang, Xuwei Zhang, Shuangnan Chen, Yangjun Shi, Hoernisa Iminniyaza
abstract: Recent DESI DR2 results suggest that dark energy may evolve with time, which motivates a re-examination of entropic cosmology. In this work, we study three representative entropic models, denoted as Models A, B, and C, corresponding to the driving terms $H^2$, $H^2+\dot H$, and $H^2+\dot H+H^4$, respectively. We establish a general framework for entropic cosmology and examine these models through early universe consistency, the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture (TCC), and the realization of Quintom-B crossing. We constrain these models using the Pantheon+ sample, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, and compare their fits to the data. For Model C, we adopt a first-order perturbative treatment in the full data analysis to maintain numerical stability in the presence of the higher-order term. We find that Model A is the simplest among the three models, but it is difficult to make it compatible with both early universe consistency and the TCC condition. Model B, which includes a derivative correction term, shows a small difference in the fit to observational data compared to Model A, and is more consistent with the theoretical constraints. Model C includes more correction terms, but does not provide a better fit to the data. The parameter region favored by observations does not fully overlap with that preferred by theoretical consistency, which suggests that entropic cosmology may require further development to achieve a self-consistent description across different cosmic epochs.
comments: 13 pages, 1 figure, 1 table, version matched the publication in Physics Letters B

title: Celia: Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions
authors: Xiaowen Zhang, Matthew Ho, Anshul Kumar, Tiziana Di Matteo, Rupert A. C. Croft, Barnabás Póczos
abstract: Cosmological hydrodynamical simulations connect observed galaxies to cosmology and the physics of galaxy formation. Each simulation is expensive, and different codes model galaxy formation in different ways. We present Celia (Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions), a self-supervised foundation model that maps catalogs of subhalos and their galaxy properties to an embedding vector for the purposes of compression and organization of astrophysical and large-scale structure information. Celia is pretrained without parameter labels on the IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid suites of CAMELS and their N-body counterparts, by reconstructing masked subhalo properties and predicting the representations of a teacher network. Simple linear models fitted to the embeddings recover $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ with $R^2=0.999$, and $\sigma_8$ and both supernova-feedback amplitudes with $R^2\geq0.97$, in all three suites. The embeddings translate well to out-of-distribution simulations such as Swift-EAGLE, a code that Celia never saw. A linear model fitted on the three training codes predicts its $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ with a correlation coefficient $r=0.985$, and linear models fitted on 20 labeled simulations reach $r\geq0.94$ for $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$, $\sigma_8$ and a supernova-feedback amplitude. We decompose the variation among the simulations of each suite into principal components of the embedding, and simple power laws of the simulation parameters describe the leading components. Celia gives simulated galaxy catalogs a shared coordinate system for simulation-based inference, emulation, the comparison of galaxy-formation models, the detection of physical degeneracies and the discovery of new astrophysical probes.
comments: 23 pages, 14 figures, 4 tables

title: A compact NH$_2$D source without NH$_3$ counterpart in the S187 high-mass star-forming region
authors: E. A. Trofimova, I. I. Zinchenko, C. Henkel, A. G. Pazukhin, A. F. Punanova, P. M. Zemlyanukha
abstract: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH$_2$D source devoid of a notable NH$_3$ counterpart, located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is $\lesssim$0.3 pc) in the S187 high-mass star-forming region. A high ammonia deuteration in such an environment is unusual. We performed observations of this area with the 20-m OSO radio telescope in several frequency ranges from $\sim$72 to $\sim$112 GHz. The area was mapped at the lower frequencies while at the higher frequencies only the position of the NH$_2$D emission peak was observed. The data were analyzed using non-LTE modeling. The data confirm a compact NH$_2$D source with a size of $\lesssim$0.2 pc. In addition, emission from about 20 molecules was detected, but only the DCO$^+$(1-0) peak coincides with the NH$_2$D clump. The clump is not associated with any known astronomical source or an NH$_3$ emission peak but the dust continuum map shows an enhancement at approximately the same position. The gas kinetic temperature derived from various indicators is $\sim$20-30 K, which possibly characterizes the surrounding material. The intrinsic NH$_2$D line width ($\sim$0.4 km/s) implies a clump with subsonic or transonic turbulence. The ortho/para NH$_2$D line intensity ratio is consistent with an abundance ratio of 3, expected from the spin statistics. The NH$_2$D/NH$_3$ abundance ratio may be $\sim$1. In general, the data hint at a compact cold gravitationally stable dense core within the warm environment, which may represent pristine material. However this picture still needs a verification with observations at a higher angular resolution.

title: From photons to neutrinos : Advancing multi-messenger modeling with Gammapy
authors: Justin Albinet, Lea Heckmann, Matteo Cerruti, Bruno Khélifi
abstract: In recent years, several astrophysical objects have been identified as potential multi-messenger photon-neutrino emitters. New instruments dedicated to the study of these two messengers have been and are still being built, achieving unprecedented sensitivity. This observational improvement increases the need for more sophisticated and precise analysis tools. Multi-wavelength and multi-messenger data fitting is crucial to constrain astrophysical models of particle acceleration and radiation mechanisms at work in these extreme environments. In this contribution, we present a novel framework dedicated to multi-wavelength and multi-messenger modeling, built within the open-source software Gammapy. The framework enables data analysis from optical up to very-high-energy gamma rays, and fitting physical models directly to instrumental counts in these wavebands, without the need of computing flux points. Focusing on blazars as a first example of a multi-messenger candidate, we showcase the performance of this tool in constraining multi-wavelength emission models, and how it reduces fitting biases. We show the results of a leptonic model that can be fitted on the fly, due to the short computing time needed. For more computing-intensive emission codes, we explore a grid-fitting approach. We evaluate the performance of the new fitting tool and present its first application to leptonic modeling of blazars. By fitting directly on photon and neutrino events, this novel approach will enable, for the first time, statistically sound constraints on the physics of multi-messenger sources.
comments: 5 pages, 5 figures, conference proceedings of Gamma 2026

title: A Candidate Binary Microlensing Event in the 2018 Gamma-Ray Flare of 3C 279
authors: Yihong Yang, Jianeng Zhou, Haibin Ren, Wei Zhu, Haiyun Zhang, Dahai Yan, Hongping Deng, Hengxiao Guo, Zhen Yan, Liang Chen, Minfeng Gu
abstract: The April 2018 gamma-ray flare of the flat-spectrum radio quasar 3C~279 exhibited sharp peaks within a broader outburst. Its rapid substructure was previously attributed to magnetic reconnection. Motivated by its distinctive temporal profile within our comparison sample of bright blazar flares and its resemblance to caustic-crossing features in optical microlensing events, we investigate a finite-source binary-microlensing interpretation. A jointly fitted model of binary-lens magnification, a smooth intrinsic flare, and Gaussian-process variability reproduces the principal double-peaked structure of the GeV light curve. The adopted local solution has a binary mass ratio of $q\simeq0.098$ and an Einstein timescale of $t_{\rm E}\simeq0.327$~d. The absolute lens mass and projected source radius depend on the lens distance and relative proper motion. The fitted geometry can correspond to a Galactic planetary-mass binary or an intervening stellar or substellar system, with different physical source sizes in each case. We present binary microlensing as a testable interpretation of this event, with the finite-source structure offering a potential probe of the compact GeV-emitting region.

title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities
authors: Michele Mancarella, Viola De Renzis, Alessandro Agapito
abstract: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.
comments: 15 pages (41 total), 8 figures (10 total). Code available at this https URL

title: Going off the (momentum) grid: A simple implementation of noncold relics in linear Boltzmann solvers
authors: Arad Nasiri, Murali Saravanan, Caio B. de S. Nascimento
abstract: Linear Boltzmann solvers typically evolve the perturbations of noncold relics, such as massive neutrinos or hot subcomponents of the dark matter, on a momentum grid, often switching to a fluid approximation on small scales for efficiency. We implement in CLASS the Dispersive Fluid Approximation (DFA), a fluid scheme that captures the scale-dependent sound speed of these species. Within the standard ncdm module, the DFA significantly outperforms the default CLASS fluid approximation in the cross and neutrino power spectra, and reduces errors in the cold dark matter power spectrum by up to an order of magnitude, while adding only 1-4% to the total runtime. We also present the first open-source implementation of the Generalized Boltzmann Hierarchy (GBH), which simplifies the implementation of noncold relics by integrating out the momentum dependence of their perturbations altogether. Combined with the DFA and tested on massive neutrinos, the GBH reproduces the matter power spectrum to better than permille accuracy and cosmological parameter constraints to better than 0.05 sigma, at a computational cost comparable to that of the standard implementation. We argue that the GBH is particularly well suited to non-thermal relics whose distribution function varies with time or across parameter space. Our implementation of both the DFA and the GBH in CLASS is publicly available at this https URL.
comments: 40 pages, 7 figures

title: Toward a Complete Interpretation of Global 21 cm Absorption Signals Using the Radio CMB
authors: Hannah Fronenberg
abstract: The global 21 cm signal is among the most direct probes of cosmic dawn, encoding information about when the first stars formed and how efficiently they heated their surroundings. However, such measurements are limited by bright Galactic foregrounds, ionospheric effects, and instrumental systematics. Even a confident detection would face a further obstacle: the brightness temperature depends on the spin temperature of the gas and the temperature of the radio background only through a single combination, so anomalous signals such as the EDGES (Bowman et al. 2018) absorption trough admit both cold gas and excess radio background interpretations. Recently, Holder et al. 2026 showed that resonant 21 cm absorption by high-redshift neutral hydrogen imprints an excess optical depth on CMB anisotropies at radio wavelengths, which depends on the spin temperature alone. Here we propose combining a measurement of the CMB hydrogen optical depth with the global signal to break this degeneracy, isolating the radio background temperature without the need for astrophysical modelling. Forecasting four interferometric configurations, we find that a compact $55 \times 55$ array of 6 m dishes observing for 4000 hours can establish an EDGES-like optical depth at $4.2\sigma$, while fiducial cosmic dawn histories require roughly an order of magnitude more collecting area. This constitutes a model-independent route to interpreting any global 21 cm detection.
comments: Note extending Holder et al. 2026 (arXiv:2605.22934); comments welcome. 9 pages, 3 figures, 1 table

figs.cap: The global 21 cm signal and the CMB attenuation it implies. Top: brightness temperature $T_{b}$ for two fiducial 21cmfast models with absorption troughs of standard depth centred at $z=17.2$ (black) and $z=12.25$ (grey), compared with the EDGES best-fit profile (red), which is deeper than either by more than a factor of two. Bottom: the corresponding fractional suppression of CMB anisotropies, $1-e^{-\tau_{\rm HI}}$, obtained from each spin temperature history via Eq. 1. A measurement of this suppression determines $T_{s}$ independently of $T_{R}$, breaking the degeneracy inherent in $T_{b}$ alone.

Forecast constraints on the template amplitude $\hat{\alpha}$ for three observational setups: Threshold (squares), Dedicated (circles; Holder et al. 33), and Robust (triangles). Constraints are obtained for three spin temperature histories chosen to bracket the plausible parameter space: the EDGES profile (deepest trough), and fiducial histories with standard-depth troughs at $z=17.2$ (early cosmic dawn) and $z=12.25$ (late). The Robust configuration confirms an EDGES-like history at better than $4\sigma$, while the fiducial histories reach $\sim 2\sigma$ at $z=12.25$ and $\sim 1\sigma$ at $z=17.2$. The anomalous scenarios are thus the most readily identified. The deeper the trough, the larger $\tau_{\rm HI}$ and the more sharply the models separate.

Required sensitivity $\Delta\hat{\alpha}$ as a function of integration time and number of 6 m dishes. Dashed contours mark the $5\sigma$ threshold for detecting the radio CMB at all, that is, rejecting the null hypothesis of no signal consistent with the CMB template. Solid contours mark the more demanding $3\sigma$ threshold for distinguishing a given spin temperature history from the alternatives. Both are shown for the EDGES profile (black) and the fiducial history (white). Detection comes slightly sooner for the fiducial case, since weaker suppression leaves $\alpha$ closer to unity, but the ordering reverses for discrimination: the EDGES threshold is reached far earlier because the model is so deep and extreme, while constraining the subtler fiducial history demands substantially more collecting area and integration time. The radio CMB is therefore an accessible near-term target in its own right, with $\tau_{\rm HI}$ science following as the array grows.

title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
authors: Yong-Kun Zhang, Yi Feng, Di Li, Jin-Tao Xie, Chao-Wei Tsai, Pei Wang, Meng-Yao Xue
abstract: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $\sigma_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magneto-ionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.
comments: 12 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJ

title: Playing CHESS with stars II. Homogeneous analysis of high-resolution optical spectra for a sample of 135 giants in 14 bulge globular clusters
authors: S. Özdemir, R. Smiljanic, J. E. Martínez Fernández, P. R. T. Coelho, F. Primas, E. Valenti
abstract: Bulge globular clusters are key tracers of the complex formation history of the Galactic bulge, as they retain information on its past star-formation episodes. Their chemical abundances serve as empirical `fossil records'' of the early evolution of the bulge. We present a homogeneous analysis of archival high-resolution UVES spectra for 135 giants in 14 Galactic bulge globular clusters. We explore the results in the context of the phenomenon of multiple stellar populations and discuss what the abundances reveal about the chemical evolution of the bulge. We employed the CHEmical Survey analysis System (CHESS) pipeline to derive atmospheric parameters on an accurate scale defined by reference stars. Abundances for Li, O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Sc, Y, Zr, Ba, Ce, Nd, and Eu were derived by spectrum synthesis. Deviations from local thermodynamic equilibrium (i.e., non-LTE or NLTE) were taken into account for Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Y, Ba, and Eu. We serendipitously discovered a Li-rich giant with A(Li) = 1.68 (after 3D NLTE corrections) in NGC 6723, which was hidden in the archival data. Our sample includes both first- and second-generation stars, as indicated by the observed spread in Na abundances. Compared to halo clusters, the bulge clusters show a lower [{\alpha}/Fe] plateau at low metallicity and a more gradual decline in [{\alpha}/Fe] toward higher metallicities. The Sc abundances are below solar and lower than in disk stars of the same metallicity. This difference could be important for solving open questions about the nucleosynthesis of this element. None of the clusters exhibit any significant spreads in heavy elements. Most clusters exhibit [Ba/Eu] \sim 0.0, indicating a contribution from both s- and r-processes. Clusters with [Fe/H] < -0.5 show negative [Ce/Nd] ratios, supporting the idea that these elements were predominantly produced by the r-process in these clusters.
comments: Accepted for publication in A&A (15 pages)

title: Cosmological lensing as a jump process
authors: Galymzhan Baltabay, Ville Vaskonen
abstract: We develop a jump-process formalism for the probability density function (PDF) of gravitational lensing fields. In the Born approximation, each lens adds a jump to the convergence $\kappa$ and the two components of the shear, making lensing a jump process in redshift. For independent lenses, the joint PDF of the lensing fields obeys a compensated Kolmogorov-Feller equation, which we solve in closed form in Fourier space and extend to clustered lenses using their two-point correlation function. A Fourier-Hankel inversion then yields the joint PDF of $\kappa$ and the shear magnitude $\gamma$, from which the magnification PDF follows, including its high-magnification tail, without sampling noise. We use these PDFs to train an updated version of the FLUMEN emulator, which makes likelihood-based inference from the full magnification distribution feasible across cosmologies. To motivate such analyses, we estimate that samples of $10^4$ Roman supernovae, $10^5$ Rubin supernovae, 300 Einstein Telescope standard sirens, and 12 LISA standard sirens could constrain the matter fluctuation amplitude $\sigma_8$ respectively to 4.8\%, 5.1\%, 8.5\%, and 19\%, with the other cosmological parameters fixed.
comments: 9 pages, 5 figures. Emulator: this https URL. Numerical solver: this https URL

title: Six New Eclipsing AM CVn Binaries from the Zwicky Transient Facility
authors: Aaron Householder, Kevin B. Burdge, Yapeng Zhang, Emma Chickles, Jan van Roestel, Matthew J. Green, Kaley Brauer, Joheen Chakraborty, Jack Dinsmore, Gabor Furesz, Juliana García-Mejía, Matthew J. Graham, Aurora Y. Kesseli, Shrinivas R. Kulkarni, Christopher Layden, Geoffrey Mo, David Osip, Roger W. Romani, Andrew Vanderburg
abstract: We present the discovery of six new eclipsing AM CVn binaries, helium-accreting ultracompact systems in which a cool donor eclipses the accreting white dwarf. The systems were found in a GPU-accelerated Box Least Squares (BLS) search of Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) photometry and have orbital periods of 39.3 to 59.9 minutes. We obtained spectroscopy with the Low Resolution Imaging Spectrometer (LRIS) on the Keck I telescope for all six systems, and every spectrum shows helium emission with no detectable hydrogen, confirming their AM CVn classification. Our discoveries increase the number of deeply eclipsing AM CVn from 11 to 17 (i.e., systems in which the accreting white dwarf is both the dominant source of optical light and eclipsed by the donor). With high-speed photometric follow-up, these systems will provide the mass ratios, inclinations, and fractional radii of both components. They will also provide new tests of AM CVn formation models and stronger constraints on the long-term evolution of these sources.
comments: 12 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ

title: Cosmological tests of chameleon dark energy with dark sector coupling
authors: Jia-Qi Wang, Zong-Kuan Guo, Shao-Jiang Wang
abstract: Recent DESI measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations favor a value of $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ different from that preferred by Planck cosmic microwave background observations. Combined with supernova data, these observations suggest an evolving dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$. As a potential solution to multiple cosmological problems, chameleon dark energy has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this work, we constrain a chameleon model in which late-time cosmic acceleration is driven by a canonical scalar field nonminimally coupled to dark matter. At early times, the scalar field evolves under the combined influence of its potential and the nonminimal coupling, and its effective mass greatly exceeds the Hubble parameter. The chameleon model with energy transfer from dark energy to dark matter yields a best-fit improvement of $\Delta\chi^2=-7.25$ relative to $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$, comparable to that for energy transfer in the opposite direction. Joint sampling over both coupling directions favors a nonzero interaction at $3.3\sigma$. Although no phantom field is introduced, the modified dark matter evolution produces an effective dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$ at $z\simeq0.5$.
comments: v1, 14 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables

title: Measuring Precipitable Water Vapor through Dual-Band GPS at Rubin Observatory
authors: Anja Weyant, W. M. Wood-Vasey, Elana K. Urbach, Sara Gelven, Marcos Tamargo-Arizmedi
abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) in Earth's atmosphere is a known source of systematic error in ground-based astronomical measurements, particularly at wavelengths greater than 7,000 angstroms. PWV produces wavelength-dependent extinction in the spectral energy distributions of observed sources. For high-precision applications, such as supernova cosmology, the transmission function must be measured accurately and precisely for each observation. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory is located in the Chilean Andes, a region known for dry conditions. However, even at this location, time-variable absorption by water vapor is a factor. Signal delays from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) offer a robust, easy, 24-hour monitoring of PWV. In this paper we present measurements from the first six months of GNSS-PWV at Rubin Observatory. We verified our analysis by replicating results from the International GNSS Service (IGS), demonstrating high consistency. We then installed and commissioned a Trimble Net R9 receiver at Allegheny Observatory for a commissioning run before it was relocated to Rubin Observatory. At Rubin Observatory we have been continuously measuring PWV since 2025 September 5. We find average PWV levels of 3.0 kg/m$^2$ in Southern Hemisphere spring (September to November) and 5.4 kg/m$^2$ in summer (December to February). The PWV at Rubin also has a clear daily variation with an amplitude of 1.2-3.8 kg/m$^2$ that is highly correlated with the east-west wind strength. We conclude that the proposed GNSS-based processing method achieves an accuracy of 0.9 kg/m$^2$ with 0.36 kg/m$^2$ precision, confirming the capability for continuous, high-temporal-resolution PWV monitoring to support demanding LSST science cases.
comments: 25 pages, 15 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to PASP

title: Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS) VIII. First interstellar detection of fully deuterated methyl cyanide
authors: A. Belloche, J. K. Jørgensen, M. N. Drozdovskaya, S. Spezzano, A. Coutens, J.-E. Lee, F. Cruz-Sáenz de Miera, D. Harsono, J.-H. Jeong, S. Maret, B. A. McGuire, P. Nazari, A. L. Plunkett, Y.-L. Yang, H.-S. Yun
abstract: Deuteration is a powerful metric to gain insight into the formation pathways of interstellar molecules in star forming regions. Our primary goal is to search for the fully deuterated form of methyl cyanide, CD3CN, in the ISM. We used a sensitive imaging spectral survey of the protostellar system L1551 IRS5 in the Taurus molecular cloud performed as part of the Large Program carried out with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) called Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS). We derived the column densities of methyl cyanide and several of its less abundant isotopologs, including deuterated ones, under the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium. All three deuterated isotopologs of methyl cyanide were detected toward the northern binary component of L1551 IRS5. In particular, we report the first interstellar detection of CD3CN. The measured D/H ratio increases by about half an order of magnitude from one deuterated isotopolog to the next, in a similar way as what was measured for methanol in several other low-mass protostars. This suggests that methyl cyanide predominantly forms like methanol on the surface of dust grains during the cold prestellar phase. However, the measured factor of 2 difference between the D/H ratios of methyl cyanide and methanol may either indicate that gas-phase processes during the warm-up stage contribute approximately equally to the production of methyl cyanide, or that methyl cyanide and its deuterated isotopologs are formed during the prestellar phase at a somewhat earlier time than methanol. Multiply deuterated isotopologs are crucial to understand the formation and inheritance of molecules in the ISM by coupling observations and astrochemical models. Unfortunately, no model has so far investigated the deuteration of methyl cyanide up to the fully deuterated form. [Abridged]
comments: Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics

title: Extension and validation of the ZPEKTR code for determining the inclination angles of Be stars
authors: Daniela Turis-Gallo, Michel Curé, Ronaldo. S. Levenhagen, Catalina Arcos, Ignacio Araya
abstract: Classical Be stars are non-supergiant B-type stars that rotate at a significant fraction of their critical velocity and are surrounded by equatorial circumstellar discs. Rapid rotation induces stellar oblateness and gravity darkening, making the emergent spectrum dependent on both the stellar parameters and the inclination angle. We assess the reliability of the ZPEKTR code for determining inclination angles across different rotation rates, identify the minimum rotation rate required for reliable estimates, and extend our previous analysis to derive consistent stellar parameters for 21 classical Be stars. We evaluated the method through noise-injection tests on synthetic spectra spanning a broad range of rotational rates and inclination angles. We constructed a grid of gravity-darkened synthetic spectra with ZPEKTR, covering the atmospheric and rotational parameter space of classical Be stars. Stellar and rotational parameters were derived through Q minimisation of the HeI 4388, 4471, and 6678 $Å$ line profiles. We applied the method to 21 classical Be stars using archival BeSOS/PUCHEROS spectra and new observations from the LCO/NRES network. The rotation rate was reliably recovered across the tested inclinations, while inclination estimates improved with increasing rotation rate. Reliable inclination estimates were obtained for V/Vc $\geq$ 0.46. For the observed sample, the derived inclination angles show excellent agreement with independent interferometric measurements, yielding $R^{2}$ = 0.985. ZPEKTR provides a promising spectroscopic method for constraining inclination angles and rotational properties in rapidly rotating massive stars. By accounting for stellar deformation and gravity darkening, it offers a practical alternative to interferometric observations and enables the analysis of larger samples of classical Be stars.
comments: Paper accepted for publication on A&A (accepted date: 21/10/2026)

title: On the Proper 3D Modeling of Orbits in Wide Binary Gravity Tests
authors: Kyu-Hyun Chae
abstract: A gravitationally-bound system of wide binary stars with precise 3D relative displacement $\mathbf{r}$ and velocity $\mathbf{v}$ can allow a Keplerian orbit reconstruction for an assumed gravitational parameter $G$. A sufficiently large sample of such systems can also be used to directly infer $G$ specific to the sample. When the sky-plane angular coordinates are (essentially) exact and the distances to the binary stars are sufficiently precise, the orbit modeling can be readily done using two internal consistency relations provided by the ratio of angular separations in R.A.\ and decl.\ and the physical sky-plane separation $s$ that must be satisfied by any Keplerian orbits. A recent study argued that treating $a$ explicitly free with an empirical prior imposed on it can dramatically change the inference of $G$ in the Chae et al.\ sample of 36 wide binaries. Here I introduce and test a Bayesian MCMC algorithm that allows $a$ to be explicitly free, and find using the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system and the Chae et al.\ sample that the explicit-$a$ algorithm with an observational constraint is fully equivalent to the implicit-$a$ algorithm with an internal consistency relation involving $s$. For the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system, I present orbits in Milgromian (MOND) as well as Newtonian gravity models obtained with the verified algorithms. I show that a recent claim of Newtonian gravity from the Chae et al.\ sample may be a consequence of using arbitrarily enlarged errors for some of $\mathbf{r}$ and/or $\mathbf{v}$. I discuss how wide binaries can be properly analyzed and modeled to probe gravity at low acceleration and test gravity models, including the necessity of deriving individual-specific parameters, the importance of follow-up observations for anomalous systems, and the relevance of Bayesian MCMC approaches.
comments: 10 pages, 5 figures

title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies
authors: D. G. Lyster, C. J. A. Howett
abstract: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.

title: UNIONS: Red and blue alignments of DESI DR1 galaxies
authors: R. Paviot, C. Murray, M. Kilbinger, C. Daley, F. Hervas-Peters, A. Corinaldi, T. de Boer, S. Guerrini, M. J. Hudson, G. S. H. Paek, L. Van Waerbeke, J. Yun
abstract: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are a dominant source of systematics in weak-lensing cosmological analyses, and direct measurements on spectroscopic samples are the primary source of priors on their amplitude. We measure the IA of galaxies from the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) as a function of colour, stellar mass, and halo mass, by cross-correlating the DESI spectroscopic catalogues with the weak-lensing shape catalogue of the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS) over up to 2400 deg$^2$. We fit the three-dimensional galaxy-galaxy and galaxy-shape multipoles of the DESI BGS, LRG, and ELG samples, split by colour and stellar mass, with the non-linear linear alignment (NLA) and the tidal alignment and tidal torquing (TATT) models. Halo masses are measured for the BGS red sample from galaxy-galaxy lensing and extended to the LRGs through the resulting stellar-to-halo mass relation. Red galaxies are strongly and radially aligned, but their alignment amplitude is not a single power law of halo mass between $6\times10^{11}$ and $3\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$: it is nearly flat at low mass and rises steeply above a break at $1.3\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$. Massive blue BGS galaxies instead show a tangential alignment, detected at $3.3\sigma$, to our knowledge the most significant detection of a non-zero alignment of blue galaxies to date, while the low-mass blue BGS galaxies and the ELGs are consistent with zero. At our current precision, the data do not favour TATT over NLA.

title: OCCAMS: A Multi-Task Learning-Based Investigation of the CMB Power Spectra
authors: Ankit Mandal, Rahul Shah, Md. Wali Hossain, Somasri Sen, Anjan A Sen, Supratik Pal
abstract: How many latent variables are needed to fit the cosmic microwave background (CMB) temperature and polarisation power spectra when a neural network is given no cosmological model, and to what extent do they map onto the standard cosmological parameters? We use multi-task learning with variational autoencoders trained on CLASS-generated spectra (TT, TE, EE) over $2\le\ell\le2500$. No cosmological model is built into the network, and the number of latent variables, $L$, is varied over $L=5$, $6$ and $7$. Their fits are compared to the Planck 2018 data using $\hat{\chi}^2$, AIC, BIC and Bayesian evidence. Their correspondence with cosmological parameters is measured with normalised mutual information post-training. The loss weights are set within a single training run by uncertainty weighting, with the weight of the disentanglement term either fixed (semi-automated, SA) or learned (completely automated, CA). The reconstruction loss is split over multipole ranges in three configurations that separate the roles of temperature and polarisation and of the low- and high-$\ell$ ranges. In four of the six combinations of configuration and strategy, the fit improves from $L=5$ to $L=6$ and not beyond, and $L=6$ is the best, or close to the best, in five of the six cases. So, six latent variables are needed, as many as the free parameters of the standard, model-dependent approach. SA gives clearer disentanglement, while CA needs no a priori choice of the disentanglement weight and has the higher evidence at $L=5$ and $6$: the two strategies are points on a trade-off between interpretability and fit to the data. Notably, the latent variables for $\tau$ and $A_s$ share almost no information in any model, consistent with large-scale polarisation separating the two, as in standard analyses. A deep-learning approach can thus give a compact, data-driven parametrisation of the CMB spectra.
comments: 13 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables, plus appendices. Comments are welcome

title: Influence of $Δ$ resonances in hyperonic neutron stars on gravitational-wave inspiral signatures
authors: Athira S., Vivek Baruah Thapa, Monika Sinha
abstract: The composition of dense matter in neutron star interiors remains uncertain, with the possible appearance of the non-strange $\Delta$ resonances providing an important source of theoretical uncertainty. In this work, we investigate the gravitational wave signatures of hyperonic neutron stars containing $\Delta$ baryons within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field framework based on the DDME2 parametrization. Within this framework, the baryons interact among themselves via mesons. For $\Delta$ baryons, the interaction is uncertain to date. We investigate how variations of the scalar and vector $\Delta-$meson couplings, subject to \(x_{\sigma\Delta}-x_{\omega\Delta}=0.2\), modify the tidal properties and inspiral gravitational-wave signals. We find that the allowed variation in the $\Delta-\sigma$ coupling leads to substantial changes in the tidal properties of the neutron stars, which in turn leave distinct imprints on the gravitational-wave waveforms, particularly in their frequency evolution, accumulated phase, and strain amplitude. These waveform differences arise through changes in tidal deformability and are not unique signatures of $\Delta$ resonances. Future gravitational-wave observations may therefore constrain the $\Delta-$meson couplings within the adopted dense-matter framework, subject to degeneracies with alternative EOS models.
comments: 16 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D
